title.raw: 卷二十五 志第十五 輿服 Volume 25 Treatises 15: Travel and Dress

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔者乘雲效駕，卷領垂衣，則黃帝皁衣纁裳，放勳彤車白馬，葉三微之序，舍寅醜之建，玄戈玉刃，作會相暉。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In antiquity they rode the clouds as their chariot and wore rolled collars with hanging robes; then the Yellow Emperor had a black upper garment and crimson lower skirt, Fangxun had a cinnabar carriage and white horses; they harmonized with the sequence of the three subtle beginnings, set aside the civil month establishment of Yin and Chou, and with dark halberd and jade blade their gatherings shone one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In the legendary age, sovereigns were pictured mounting the clouds as a chariot and governing in loosely draped robes. The Yellow Emperor wore black above and reddish brown below; Yao (Fangxun) rode a vermilion chariot drawn by white horses. Rulers aligned the calendar with the “three subtle” sequence and moved away from taking Yin or Chou as the first month; black halberds and jade blades flashed together in court, each emblem answering the next in splendor.

sentences.zh: 若乃參旗分景，帝車含曜，又所以營衛南宮，增華北極。

translations.literal: As for Orion’s banner dividing the sun’s shadow and the Imperial Chariot holding radiance, these were again the means to guard the Southern Palace and add glory to the Northern Pole.
translations.idiomatic: The constellations Orion’s Belt and the Celestial Chariot mark off daylight and gather starlight—emblems, as it were, for protecting the southern celestial palace and crowning the northern pivot of the sky.

sentences.zh: 《月令》季夏之月，「命婦官染彩」，赬丹班次，各有品章矣。

translations.literal: In the “Monthly Ordinances,” for the last month of summer it says, “Order the women’s offices to dye the colors,” and cinnabar and red were ranked in order, each with its grades and patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances for late summer command the palace dyers to set the palette; shades of cinnabar and vermilion were sequenced by rank, each hue carrying its regulated pattern.

sentences.zh: 高旗有日月之象，式視有威儀之選，衣兼鞙珮，衡載鳴和，是以閑邪屏棄，不可入也。

translations.literal: High banners bore the images of sun and moon; the style of the chariot crosspiece showed selection of majesty; garments were joined with girdle-pendants, and the yoke-bar carried sounding chimes—thereby idle evil was barred and cast out and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Tall standards carried sun and moon; the chariot’s balancing crosspiece proclaimed dignity; robes were set off by belt ornaments, and the yoke bore harmonizing bells—together they shut out wickedness so that nothing base could slip through.

sentences.zh: 若乃正名百物，補緝四維，疏懷山之水，靜傾天之害，功尤彰者飾彌煥，德愈盛者服彌尊，莫不質良，用成其美。

translations.literal: As for rectifying the names of the myriad things, patching the four cords, dredging the waters that threaten to engulf mountains, and quieting harms that would tilt the sky—where merit was especially manifest, ornament became especially brilliant; where virtue grew greater, dress grew more exalted; none failed to be of good substance, thereby completing their beauty.
translations.idiomatic: When rulers set the world in order—sorting names, binding the four directions, taming floods that could swallow hills, and checking disasters that seemed to shake the heavens—the greater the achievement, the richer the regalia; the deeper the virtue, the loftier the costume. Everything was made of fine materials so that splendor matched substance.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「明試以功，車服以庸。

translations.literal: The Documents says: “Clearly try them by their tasks; chariots and robes according to merit.”
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents reads: “Test officers plainly by their work, and reward them with chariots and robes in proportion to their service.”

sentences.zh: 」「《禮記》曰：「鸞車，有虞氏之路也。

translations.literal: ” “The Record of Rites says: “The bell-bird carriage was the lu of the Youyu clan.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Record of Rites continues: “The luan carriage was the ritual chariot of the Shun (Youyu) house.”

sentences.zh: 鉤車，夏後氏之路也。

translations.literal: The hook carriage was the lu of the Xia house.
translations.idiomatic: The “hook” carriage was the ritual chariot of the Xia kings.

sentences.zh: 大路，殷路也。

translations.literal: The great lu was the lu of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The great chariot was the Shang (Yin) ritual carriage.

sentences.zh: 乘路，周路也。

translations.literal: The sheng lu was the lu of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The “sheng” carriage was the Zhou ritual chariot.

sentences.zh: 」而韍火山龍，以通其意。

translations.literal: ” And with fu, fire, mountain, and dragon, they communicated their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: ” On robes, axe-shaped fu, fire, mountain, and dragon motifs conveyed the ruler’s intentions through regulated symbolism.

sentences.zh: 前史以為，聖人見鳥獸容貌，草木英華，始創衣冠，而玄黃殊采；

translations.literal: Earlier historians held that the sages, observing the forms of birds and beasts and the splendor of plants, first created caps and robes, so that black and yellow showed different colors;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier writers thought the sages invented hats and gowns after studying the shapes of birds and beasts and the brilliance of plants, dividing garments into dark and bright colors.

sentences.zh: 見秋蓬孤轉，杓觿旁建，乃作輿輪，而方圓異則。

translations.literal: seeing autumn thistledown whirl alone and the ladle and girdle-pick set to one side, they then made carts and wheels, so that square and round had different norms.
translations.idiomatic: Watching thistledown spin in the wind and noting how the Dipper and girdle-hook stars stand askew, they devised carts and wheels with distinct rules for square hubs and round felloes.

sentences.zh: 遇物成象，觸類興端。

translations.literal: Encountering things, they formed images; touching categories, they raised beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: Each thing they met suggested a design; each kind inspired a new institution.

sentences.zh: 周因于殷，其來已舊。

translations.literal: Zhou inherited from Yin; its origin was already old.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou built on Shang practice; the lineage of these forms was already ancient.

sentences.zh: 成王之會，壇垂陰羽，五方之盛，有八十物者焉。

translations.literal: At King Cheng’s assembly, the altar hung dark feathers, and among the splendors of the five directions there were eighty kinds of things.
translations.idiomatic: At King Cheng’s great gathering of lords, the ritual mound bore somber plumes, and the regalia of the five regions displayed some eighty emblematic items.

sentences.zh: 宗馬鳥旌，奚往不格，殷公、曹叔，此焉低首。

translations.literal: With ancestral horses and bird streamers, whither they went none resisted; the Duke of Yin and Prince Cao of here bowed their heads.
translations.idiomatic: With royal horses and bird-decked banners, every march commanded submission—even lords like the Duke of Yin and Prince Cao had to lower their heads before such majesty.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》，巾車氏建大赤以朝，大白以戎。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the chariot office raises the great cinnabar standard for court and the great white for war.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou ritual specifies the chariot master’s raising a great scarlet banner for audiences and a great white one for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 雅制弘多，式遵遺範，賓入異憲，師行殊則，是以有嚴有翼，用光其武，鉤膺鞗革，乃暢其文。

translations.literal: The elegant models were many; they followed the surviving patterns; guests entered under different statutes, armies marched under different rules—therefore there was awe and wing-like support, thereby displaying their martial brilliance; hooked breast-strap and leather reins, thereby giving full play to their civil refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Models multiplied, yet all echoed antique precedent: guests were received under one set of rules, campaigns under another, so court looked stern and supportive while war gear flashed power—breast-straps of bronze, supple leathers—yet the same system lent polish to civil display.

sentences.zh: 六服之冕，五時之路，王之常制，各有等差。

translations.literal: The caps of the six domains and the chariots of the five seasons were the king’s constant institutions, each with its gradations.
translations.idiomatic: The six grades of feudal caps and the five seasonal chariot colors were fixed parts of royal ceremony, each step distinguished by rank.

sentences.zh: 逮禮業雕訛，人情馳爽，諸侯征伐，憲度淪亡，一紫亂于齊飾，長纓混于鄒玩。

translations.literal: When rites and enterprises were carved awry and human hearts raced dissolute, the feudal lords campaigned in arms and statutes perished; one purple threw Qi’s dress into confusion, and long tassels mingled with Zou’s trifles.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as ritual frayed and ambition ran wild, vassals fought one another and regulations collapsed—a single fashionable purple threw Qi’s wardrobe into chaos, while absurdly long hat cords became playthings in Zou.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「君子其學也博，其服也鄉。

translations.literal: Confucius said: “The gentleman’s learning is broad; his dress follows his home village.”
translations.idiomatic: Confucius remarked: “The noble man studies widely, yet his clothing stays appropriate to the customs of his own place.”

sentences.zh: 」若乃豪傑不經，庶人幹典，彯鷸冠于鄭伯之門，躡珠履于春申之第。

translations.literal: ” As for heroes who did not follow the classics, commoners who violated the canons, sporting kingfisher caps at the Earl of Zheng’s gate and treading pearl slippers in Lord Chunshen’s hall—
translations.idiomatic: ” Yet bold men ignored precedent and commoners flouted sumptuary law—some flaunted kingfisher-feather caps at the Zheng ruler’s gate, others wore pearl-sewn shoes in Lord Chunshen’s mansion.

sentences.zh: 及秦皇並國，攬其餘軌，豐貂東至，獬豸南來，又有玄旗皁旒之制，旄頭罕車之飾，寫九王之廷於咸陽北阪，車輿之彩，各樹其文，所謂秦人大備，而陳戰國之後車者也。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin united the states, he gathered what remained of their tracks; rich sable came from the east, xiezhi caps from the south; moreover there were regulations of black banners and dark tassels, ornaments of yak-tail lances and rare chariots; he copied the courts of the nine kings on the north slope of Xianyang; the colors of chariots each planted their patterns—this is what is called the Qin having full panoply and lining up the rear chariots of the Warring States.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Shi Huang conquered the realm, he swept up every regional fashion: sable streamed in from the east, “unicorn” judge’s caps from the south, along with black standards, sable tassels, yak-tail lances, and exotic escort cars. He staged the nine kings’ courts on Xianyang’s north terrace, each chariot type painted in its own motif—what later writers mean by “Qin had everything, down to the baggage train of the Warring States.”

sentences.zh: 及凝脂布網，經書咸燼，削滅三代，以金根為帝軫，除棄六冕，以袀玄為祭服。

translations.literal: When congealed grease spread its net and the classics were all burned, he cut away the Three Dynasties, took the metal-root as the emperor’s axle-tree, cast off the six crowns, and used plain dark silk for sacrificial robes.
translations.idiomatic: After the bibliocaust, when even classics fed the flames, he tried to erase the Three Dynasties at a stroke: the “metal-root” chariot became the imperial norm, the six ancient crown types were junked, and sacrifices were conducted in austere unembroidered black.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，既因秦制。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor entered the Pass, he already followed Qin institutions.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bang entered the Qin heartland, he initially kept the Qin ceremonial wardrobe and chariot codes.

sentences.zh: 世宗挺英雄之略，總文景之資，揚霓拂翳，皮軒記鼓，橫汾河而祠后土，登甘泉而祭昊天，奉常獻儀，謂之大駕，車千乘而騎萬匹。

translations.literal: The Shizong displayed a heroic strategy, marshaled the resources of Wen and Jing, raised rainbow canopies brushing the shade, leather-screen chariots with inscribed drums, crossed the Fen River to sacrifice to Hou Tu, ascended Sweet Dew to sacrifice to August Heaven; the Minister of Ceremonies presented the models called the Grand Escort—thousands of chariots and ten thousand mounts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu (Han Shizong) deployed heroic ambition on the accumulated wealth of the Wen–Jing era: iridescent banners parted the haze, leather-screen cars rolled with painted drums, he forded the Fen to worship Earth on the square mound and climbed Sweet Dew Mound to honor Heaven. The court of ritual offered the “grand chariot” array—legend speaks of a thousand cars and ten thousand riders.

sentences.zh: 至於成帝，以幸姬趙飛燕置屬車間豹尾中，又楊雄所謂彏天狼之威弧，張曜日之靈旄，駢羅列布，霧集雲合者也。

translations.literal: As for Emperor Cheng, he placed his favorite, Zhao Feiyan, among the attendant cars within the leopard-tail cordon; moreover it was what Yang Xiong called drawing the mighty bow of Sirius and spreading sun-bright spirit banners, ranged side by side, gathering like fog and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng even tucked his favorite Zhao Feiyan’s carriage inside the leopard-tail escort—exactly the sort of spectacle Yang Xiong mocked: banners like Sirius’s war-bow, pennons blazing like the sun, vehicles massed “like mist and cloud.”

sentences.zh: 于後王氏擅朝，武車常軔，赤眉之亂，文物無遺。

translations.literal: Afterward the Wang clan monopolized the court, war chariots constantly blocked the roads, and in the Red Eyebrows rebellion nothing of the regalia survived.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Wang family hijacked government, armored columns clogged the highways, and when the Red Eyebrows swept through, the old Han ceremonial gear vanished entirely.

sentences.zh: 建武十三年，吳漢平蜀，始送葆車輿輦，充庭之飾，漸以周備。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jianwu, Wu Han pacified Shu and began to send treasure chariots and palanquins, court-filling ornaments, which gradually became complete.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Guangwu’s thirteenth Jianwu year, after Wu Han conquered Shu, captured Shu ceremonial wagons and litters reached the capital; bit by bit the court regained a full set of display vehicles.

sentences.zh: 明帝采《周官》、《禮記》，更服袞章，天子冠通天而佩玉璽。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming took the Zhou Offices and the Record of Rites and revised the robe with dragon roundels; the Son of Heaven capped himself with the “piercing-heaven” crown and wore the jade seal on his belt.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Di reworked court dress from the Zhou Offices and the Record of Rites, adopting the dragon-embroidered sacrificial robe; the emperor wore the tall tongtian (“pierce-heaven”) crown and carried the jade seal at his waist.

sentences.zh: 魏明以黼黻之美，有疑於僭，於是隨章儐略，而捐者半焉。

translations.literal: Wei Ming Di, because the beauty of axe-and-fu embroidery seemed dangerously close to usurpation, then followed chapter and rank in simplifying the regalia, and half of what had been worn was cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui (Wei Ming Di), fearing that rich axe-and-fu brocade smacked of overreach, pared the wardrobe to match statute, discarding roughly half the old finery.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆奏曰：「改正朔、殊徽號者，帝王所以神明其政，變民耳目也。

translations.literal: Gao Tang Long memorialized: “Changing the first month of the year and altering emblems is how emperors make their government numinous and transform the people’s eyes and ears.”
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tang Long argued: “Revising the calendar and regalia is how a ruler signals a new order and resets what the people see and hear.”

sentences.zh: 」帝從其議，改青龍五年為景初元年，服色尚黃，從地正也。

translations.literal: ” The emperor followed his proposal, changed the fifth year of Qinglong to the first year of Jingchu, honored yellow in dress colors, following the earth’s correct alignment.
translations.idiomatic: ” The throne agreed: Qinglong year five became Jingchu year one, court color turned to yellow in deference to the “earth” alignment of the calendar.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝接天人之貺，開典午之基，受終之禮，皆如唐虞故事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of the Shizu line received Heaven and man’s gift, opened the foundation of the Jin (the “典午”), and the ceremony of receiving the mandate all followed the precedents of Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan, the martial founding emperor, accepted heaven’s mandate and men’s allegiance, laid the Jin dynastic base—his accession rites consciously echoed the legendary abdications of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 晉氏金行，而服色尚赤，豈有司失其傳歟！

translations.literal: The Jin house belongs to the metal phase, yet dress color honored red—could it be that the officials lost the transmission?
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s element was metal, yet court dress favored red—did the ministry simply mishandle the old theory?

sentences.zh: 玉、金、象、革、木等路，是為五路，並天子之法車，皆硃班漆輪，畫為文。

translations.literal: Jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood chariots—these are the five lu—and together they are the Son of Heaven’s statutory chariots; all have vermillion-spotted lacquered wheels painted with patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The five ritual chariots—jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood—form the emperor’s canonical set; each rides on red-flecked lacquer wheels painted with designs.

sentences.zh: 三十幅，法月之數；

translations.literal: Thirty spokes match the number of the month;
translations.idiomatic: Thirty spokes match the lunar count;

sentences.zh: 重轂，貳轄，以赤油，廣八寸，長三尺，注地，系兩軸頭，謂之飛軨。

translations.literal: double hubs, paired linchpins, with red oil, eight inches wide and three feet long, dropping to the ground, tied at both axle ends—these are called flying linchpins.
translations.idiomatic: They use paired hub drums and twin linchpins, draped with red-oil cloth eight inches broad and three feet long, hanging to the ground and lashed at each axle tip—the “flying” linchpin screens.

sentences.zh: 金薄繆龍繞之為輿倚較，較重，為文獸伏軾，龍首銜軛，左右吉陽筩，鸞雀立衡，文畫轅及轓。

translations.literal: Thin gold sheets with intertwining dragons coil as chariot-side leaning-bars; the leaning-bars are heavy; patterned beasts crouch on the shield-grip; dragon heads hold the yoke; auspicious tubes stand left and right on the crossbar; luan birds stand on the balance; patterns are painted on the shaft and fenders.
translations.idiomatic: Gold foil dragons wrap the side rails; heavy curved “leaning” bars bear molded beasts on the front shield; dragon heads bite the yoke; lucky tubes flank the crossbar; luan birds perch on the pivot; shaft and fenders carry painted motifs.

sentences.zh: 青蓋，黃為裏，謂之黃屋。

translations.literal: A green canopy with yellow inside is called the yellow house.
translations.idiomatic: The green outer canopy lined in yellow is the imperial “yellow house.”

sentences.zh: 金華施橑末，橑二十八以象宿。

translations.literal: Golden splendor is applied at the rafter ends; twenty-eight rafters symbolize the lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Gilded caps finish twenty-eight canopy ribs to mirror the lunar lodges.

sentences.zh: 兩箱之後，皆玳瑁為鶤翅，加以金銀雕飾，故世人亦謂之金鶤車。

translations.literal: Behind both side boxes, hawk wings are made of tortoiseshell with gold and silver carving, so worldly people also call it the golden-hawk chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Tortoiseshell “hawk wings” trim the rear of each side box, inlaid with gold and silver—hence the nickname “golden hawk car.”

sentences.zh: 斜注旂旗于車之左，又加棨戟于車之右，皆橐而施之。

translations.literal: Banners are slanted onto the left of the chariot, and halberds are added to the right, both sheathed and mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Slanted pennons ride on the car’s left, cased halberds on the right, both fixed in place.

sentences.zh: 棨戟韜以黻繡，上為亞字，系大蛙蟆幡。

translations.literal: The halberds are sheathed in fu-and-xi embroidery, with an “ya” character above, tying a great toad banner.
translations.idiomatic: Halberd quivers wear black-and-white embroidered slips marked with a ya-shaped cross motif and fasten a large toad pennon.

sentences.zh: 軛長丈餘。

translations.literal: The yoke is over a zhang in length.
translations.idiomatic: The yoke pole runs more than ten feet long.

sentences.zh: 於戟之杪，以犛牛尾，大如鬥，置左騑馬軛上，是為左纛。

translations.literal: At the tip of the halberd, a yak tail as large as a dou is placed on the left outer horse’s yoke—this is the left yak-tail banner.
translations.idiomatic: A yak tail the size of a bucket tops the halberd shaft and is fixed to the left trace horse’s yoke—the imperial “left yak-tail” ensign.

sentences.zh: 轅皆曲向上，取《禮緯》「山車垂句」之義，言不揉而能自曲。

translations.literal: The shafts all bend upward, taking from the Ritual Weft “mountain chariot hanging hook” the meaning that they bend without being steamed.
translations.idiomatic: The shafts curve upward, echoing the omen text about “mountain cars” and drooping hooks—meaning they arc naturally without steam-bending.

sentences.zh: 玉、金、象三路，各以其物飾車，因以為名。

translations.literal: The jade, gold, and ivory three chariots each ornament the car with its material and thereby take its name.
translations.idiomatic: The jade, gold, and ivory cars are named for the materials that sheath them.

sentences.zh: 革者漆革，木者漆木。

translations.literal: Leather means lacquered leather; wood means lacquered wood.
translations.idiomatic: The leather car is lacquered hide; the wood car is lacquered timber.

sentences.zh: 其制，玉路最尊，建太常，十有二旒，九仞委地，畫日月升龍，以祀天。

translations.literal: In their system, the jade lu is highest; it raises the Grand Constant with twelve tassels, nine ren trailing to the ground, painting sun, moon, and ascending dragon, to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Of the five, the jade chariot ranks first: it flies the Grand Constant banner with twelve streamers, nine ren of silk brushing earth, painted with sun, moon, and climbing dragon—for suburban worship of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 金路建大旂，九旒，以會萬國之賓，亦以賜上公及王子母弟。

translations.literal: The gold lu raises the great banner with nine tassels, to assemble the myriad states’ guests, and is also conferred on senior dukes and the king’s younger brothers by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: The gold car bears a nine-tasseled great banner for feasting the lords of all regions and may be awarded to chief dukes and the ruler’s uterine brothers.

sentences.zh: 象路建大赤，通赤無畫，所以視朝，亦以賜諸侯。

translations.literal: The ivory lu raises the great cinnabar, entirely red without painting, by which to hold court, and is also conferred on feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The ivory car flies a plain scarlet great banner—used for ordinary audiences and granted to vassal kings.

sentences.zh: 革路建大白，以即戎兵事，亦以賜四鎮諸侯。

translations.literal: The leather lu raises the great white, for going to war on military affairs, and is also conferred on the four-guard marquises.
translations.idiomatic: The leather car carries the great white standard for campaign and is given to the “four guardian” marquises.

sentences.zh: 木路建大麾，以田獵，其麾色黑，亦以賜籓國。

translations.literal: The wood lu raises the great black-falcon banner, for hunting; its banner is black in color, and is also conferred on frontier states.
translations.idiomatic: The wood car hoists a black hawk banner for the hunt and may be presented to outlying principalities.

sentences.zh: 玉路駕六黑馬，余四路皆駕四馬，馬並以黃金為文髦，插以翟尾。

translations.literal: The jade lu is hitched to six black horses; the remaining four chariots are all hitched to four horses; the horses all have golden patterned manes with pheasant tail plumes inserted.
translations.idiomatic: The jade chariot draws six black horses; the other four draw teams of four; every horse wears gold-threaded forelocks and pheasant-tail plumes.

sentences.zh: 象鑣而鏤錫，錫在馬面，所謂當顱者也。

translations.literal: They have elephant-shaped cheek-pieces and openwork xi tin; the xi is on the horse’s face—what is called the “forehead metal.”
translations.idiomatic: Cheek-straps end in elephant motifs and carry pierced forehead ornaments (xi)—the metal plate on the horse’s brow.

sentences.zh: 金㚇而方釳，

translations.literal: Gold zong and square xi,
translations.idiomatic: Gold zong bosses and square xi cheek plates,

sentences.zh: 〈金㚇謂以金㚇為文。

translations.literal: 〈Gold zong means using gold zong as pattern.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Commentary: “Gold zong” means the bosses are patterned in gold.

sentences.zh: 釳以鐵為之，其大三寸，中央兩頭高，如山形，貫中以翟尾而結著之也。〉

translations.literal: The xi is made of iron, three inches across at the center, both ends raised like a mountain shape, pierced through with pheasant tail tied and fixed.〉
translations.idiomatic: The xi plate is iron, three inches through the middle with raised ends like a peak, threaded with pheasant tail and bound fast.〉

sentences.zh: 繁纓赤罽易茸，金就十有二。

translations.literal: Thick tassels of red felt with easy fluff; twelve golden finials.
translations.idiomatic: Breast tassels of red felt with soft pile, set with twelve gold studs.

sentences.zh: 繁纓，馬飾纓，在馬膺前，如索裙。

translations.literal: Thick tassels are the horse’s ornamental tassels, on the horse’s chest before the saddle, like a rope skirt.
translations.idiomatic: The “thick tassels” are the chest ornaments—hanging before the saddle like a cord skirt.

sentences.zh: 五路皆有錫鸞之飾，和鈴之響，鉤膺玉瓖，鉤膺，即繁纓也。

translations.literal: The five chariots all have xi and luan ornaments, and the sound of harmony bells; hooked breast-strap and jade huan; hooked breast-strap is the same as the thick tassels.
translations.idiomatic: All five cars carry forehead plaques and luan motifs, harmonizing bells, bronze breast-straps, and jade belt-rings—the breast-strap is the same piece as the “thick tassel” array.

sentences.zh: 瓖，馬帶玦名也。

translations.literal: Huan is the name of the horse’s belt ring.
translations.idiomatic: The huan is the jade ring on the harness band.

sentences.zh: 龍輈華轙，輈，車轅也，頭為龍象。

translations.literal: Dragon shaft and splendid yi; the shaft is the chariot pole, its head made in the image of a dragon.
translations.idiomatic: The pole ends in a dragon head; “yi” refers to the splendid collar hardware.

sentences.zh: 轙，謂車衡上環受鸞者也。

translations.literal: Yi means the ring on the chariot crossbar that receives the luan.
translations.idiomatic: Here “yi” is the ring on the yoke that catches the luan bird finial.

sentences.zh: 硃幩。

translations.literal: Cinnabar fen.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar-dyed fen screens.

sentences.zh: 幩，飾也，人君以硃纏鑣扇汗，以為飾也。

translations.literal: Fen is ornament; the ruler uses cinnabar thread to wrap the cheek-piece fan-screen for sweat, taking it as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: “Fen” means decoration: the emperor wraps the cheek-guards’ sweat screens in vermilion thread as trim.

sentences.zh: 法駕行則五路各有所主，不懼出；

translations.literal: When the statutory escort travels, each of the five chariots has its master and is not rashly taken out;
translations.idiomatic: On a statutory progress each of the five ritual cars has its assigned role and is not deployed at random;

sentences.zh: 臨軒大會則陳乘輿車輦旌鼓於其殿庭。

translations.literal: when there is a great assembly facing the hall, then the imperial chariots, palanquins, banners, and drums are arrayed in that hall’s courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: at a great court audience the imperial cars, litters, standards, and drums line the forecourt.

sentences.zh: 車，坐乘者謂之安車，倚乘者謂之立車，亦謂之高車。

translations.literal: Among chariots, those in which one sits to ride are called peace chariots; those in which one leans to ride are called standing chariots, also called high chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots meant for seated riding are “peace cars”; those for standing riders are “standing cars,” also called high cars.

sentences.zh: 案《周禮》，惟王后有安車也，王亦無之。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, only the queen had a peace chariot; the king also did not have one.
translations.idiomatic: The classic Zhou text grants a seated carriage only to the queen—not even to the king.

sentences.zh: 自漢以來制乘輿，乃有之。

translations.literal: From Han onward, in instituting the imperial train, there then were such chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Han codified the imperial cortège did the emperor acquire them.

sentences.zh: 有青立車、青安車、赤立車、赤安車、黃立車、黃安車、白立車、白安車、黑立車、黑安車，合十乘，名為五時車，俗謂之五帝車。

translations.literal: There are green standing, green peace, red standing, red peace, yellow standing, yellow peace, white standing, white peace, black standing, black peace—ten chariots in all—called the five-season chariots, vulgarly termed the Five Emperors’ cars.
translations.idiomatic: The suite includes green, red, yellow, white, and black versions in both standing and seated styles—ten cars altogether—known as the five-season set, popularly called the “Five Thearchs’ chariots.”

sentences.zh: 天子所禦則駕六，其餘並駕四。

translations.literal: What the Son of Heaven personally drives is hitched to six; the rest are all hitched to four.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s own car draws six horses; the rest use four-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 建旂十二，各如車色。

translations.literal: Twelve banners are raised, each matching its chariot’s color.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pennons fly, each dyed to match its car.

sentences.zh: 立車則正豎其旂，安車則邪注。

translations.literal: On standing chariots the banner is set straight upright; on peace chariots it is slanted.
translations.idiomatic: Standing cars carry vertical poles; peace cars tilt their standards.

sentences.zh: 駕馬，馬亦各隨五時之色，白馬則朱其尾，左右騑驂，金㚇鏤錫，黃屋左纛，如金根之制，行則從後。

translations.literal: The horses are harnessed, the horses also following the five seasons’ colors; white horses have their tails dyed vermillion; left and right trace and side horses have gold zong and openwork xi, yellow house and left yak-tail, like the metal-root system; when moving they follow behind.
translations.idiomatic: Horses are caparisoned to the five seasonal hues—white horses get vermilion tails; outriggers wear gold bosses and openwork xi, the yellow-lined canopy and left yak-tail, matching the metal-root style, and fall in behind when the train moves.

sentences.zh: 五牛旗，平吳後所造，以五牛建旗，車設五牛，青赤在左，黃在中，白黑在右。

translations.literal: The five-ox banner was made after the pacification of Wu; with five oxen it raises the banner; the chariot sets five oxen, green and red on the left, yellow in the center, white and black on the right.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, Jin introduced the five-ox standard: five oxen support the flag, green and red to the left, yellow in the middle, white and black to the right.

sentences.zh: 豎旗于牛背，行則使人輿之。

translations.literal: The banner is set vertical on the ox’s back; when moving, people carry it in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: The pole stands upright on the ox; on the march bearers lift it in a portable frame.

sentences.zh: 牛之為義，蓋取其負重致遠而安穩也。

translations.literal: As for the ox’s significance, it probably takes from its bearing weight and reaching far in stability.
translations.idiomatic: Oxen were chosen for their steady strength over long distances.

sentences.zh: 旗常纏不舒，所謂德車結旌也。

translations.literal: The regular banners stay wound and are not unfurled—this is what is called the virtue chariot tying its streamers.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime the pennons stay furled—what ritualists call the “virtue car” with knotted streamers.

sentences.zh: 天子親戎則舒，謂武車綏旌也。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven personally goes to war, then they are unfurled—this is called the martial chariot relaxing its streamers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor takes the field, they spread— the “martial car” with loosened streamers.

sentences.zh: 金根車，駕四馬，不建旗幟，其上如畫輪車，下猶金根之飾。

translations.literal: The metal-root chariot is hitched to four horses, does not raise banners, its upper part like a painted-wheel chariot, its lower part still metal-root ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The metal-root car uses four horses and no lofty standards; its upperworks resemble a painted pleasure cart, its undercarriage the metal-root trim.

sentences.zh: 耕根車，駕四馬，建赤旂，十有二旒，天子親耕所乘者也。

translations.literal: The ploughing-root chariot is hitched to four horses, raises a red banner with twelve tassels, and is what the Son of Heaven personally rides for the ploughing rite.
translations.idiomatic: The ploughing chariot, four horses, flies a twelve-tasseled red banner—the car the emperor rides to the spring furrow ritual.

sentences.zh: 一名芝車，一名三蓋車。

translations.literal: One name is zhi chariot, one name is three-canopy chariot.
translations.idiomatic: It is also called the “fungus” car or the “triple-canopy” car.

sentences.zh: 置耒耜於軾上。

translations.literal: Plow and spade are placed on the shield-grip.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial plough and spade rest on the front rail.

sentences.zh: 魏景初元年，改正朔，易服色，色尚黃，牲用白，戎事乘黑首白馬，建大赤之旂，朝會則建大白，行殷之時也。

translations.literal: In Wei’s first Jingchu year, the first month was corrected, dress colors changed, color honored yellow, victims used white, for military affairs they rode black-headed white horses, raised the great cinnabar banner, at court meetings raised the great white, enacting Yin’s season.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei’s Jingchu inaugural year the calendar and palette were revised: yellow dominated dress, white sacrificial beasts, black-maned white horses for war, great scarlet banners on campaign, great white at audiences—deliberately echoing the Yin alignment.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，有司奏：「宜如有虞遵唐故事，皆用前代正朔服色，其金根、耕根車，並以建赤旗。

translations.literal: In Taishi second year, the offices memorialized: “It is fitting, like Yu following Tang’s story, to use the former dynasty’s first month and dress colors; the metal-root and ploughing-root chariots should both raise built scarlet flags.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taishi year two ministers argued: “We should imitate Shun deferring to Tang and keep the previous dynasty’s calendar and colors; metal-root and ploughing cars ought both to fly built scarlet banners.”

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: ” The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 輦，案自漢以來為人君之乘，魏晉禦小出即乘之。

translations.literal: The palanquin: according to custom from Han onward it was the ruler’s conveyance; Wei and Jin used it for the emperor’s short outings.
translations.idiomatic: The litter had been the sovereign’s short-trip vehicle since Han; Wei and Jin emperors routinely rode it for informal exits from the palace.

sentences.zh: 戎車，駕四馬，天子親戎所乘者也。

translations.literal: The war chariot is hitched to four horses and is what the Son of Heaven personally rides when going to war.
translations.idiomatic: The war car, four horses, carries the emperor onto the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 載金鼓、羽旗、幢翳，置弩於軾上，其建矛麾悉斜注。

translations.literal: It loads metal drums, feather banners, canopy screens; a crossbow is set on the shield-grip; its raised spears and banners are all slanted.
translations.idiomatic: It bears bronze drums, feathered standards, sun-shades; a crossbow mounts on the rail; spears and pennons all slant forward.

sentences.zh: 獵車，駕四馬，天子校獵所乘也。

translations.literal: The hunt chariot is hitched to four horses and is what the Son of Heaven rides for the encirclement hunt.
translations.idiomatic: The hunting car, four horses, serves the emperor at the great battue.

sentences.zh: 重輞漫輪，繆龍繞之。

translations.literal: Heavy rim, fully covered wheel, intertwining dragons winding it.
translations.idiomatic: It has a broad rim, fully shod wheel, and coiling dragon paint.

sentences.zh: 一名闒戟車，一名蹋豬車。

translations.literal: One name is halberd-bar chariot, one name is pig-tread chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Also called the “halberd-rack” car or colloquially the “pig-stomper.”

sentences.zh: 魏文帝改名蹋獸車。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi changed the name to beast-tread chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi renamed it the “beast-tread” vehicle.

sentences.zh: 《記》云「國君不乘奇車」，奇車亦獵車也。

translations.literal: The Record says, “A state ruler does not ride odd chariots”; odd chariots are also hunt chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The classic warns that “a lord of a state does not ride strange cars”—those “strange” vehicles meant hunt wagons.

sentences.zh: 古天子獵則乘木輅，後人代以獵車也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven for the hunt rode the wooden lu; later men substituted the hunt chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings hunted from the plain wood ritual car; later courts swapped in the dedicated hunt carriage.

sentences.zh: 游車，九乘，駕四，先驅之乘是也。

translations.literal: Patrol chariots, nine in number, hitched to four, are the vanguard mounts.
translations.idiomatic: Nine “patrol” cars, each with four horses, form the advance screen of the train.

sentences.zh: 雲罕車，駕四。

translations.literal: The cloud-net chariot is hitched to four horses.
translations.idiomatic: The yun-han screen car rides four horses.

sentences.zh: 皮軒車，駕四，以獸皮為軒。

translations.literal: The leather-screen chariot is hitched to four horses; it uses animal hide for the screen.
translations.idiomatic: The leather-canopied escort wagon, team of four, lines its screen with pelts.

sentences.zh: 鸞旗車，駕四，先輅所載也。

translations.literal: The luan-banner chariot is hitched to four horses; it is what the forward lu carries.
translations.idiomatic: The luan-feather banner car, four horses, rides with the vanguard train.

sentences.zh: 鸞旗者，謂析羽旄而編之，列系幢傍也。

translations.literal: As for the luan banner, it means splitting yak-tail plumes and weaving them, arrayed and tied beside the canopy post.
translations.idiomatic: The “luan” standard is built from split yak plumes braided together and lashed along the canopy uprights.

sentences.zh: 建華車，駕四，凡二乘，行則分居左右。

translations.literal: The splendor-blossom chariot is hitched to four horses; in all there are two; when moving they are divided to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Two “splendid blossom” cars, each with four horses, deploy one to each side when the column moves.

sentences.zh: 輕車，駕二，古之戰車也。

translations.literal: The light chariot is hitched to two horses; it is the ancient war chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Light strike cars use two-horse teams—the old Zhou-style fighting wagon.

sentences.zh: 前後二十乘，分居左右。

translations.literal: Twenty chariots front and rear are divided to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty such cars split fore and aft between the left and right files.

sentences.zh: 輿輪洞硃，不巾不蓋，建矛戟麾幢，置弩箙於軾上。

translations.literal: The body and wheels are wholly cinnabar; there is no curtain and no canopy; spears, halberds, banners, and pennons are raised; a crossbow case is placed on the shield-grip.
translations.idiomatic: They are painted solid vermilion, open-topped, bristling with spears, halberds, and streamers, with a crossbow case fixed to the front rail.

sentences.zh: 大駕法駕出，射聲校尉、司馬、吏士、戰士載，以次屬車。

translations.literal: When the grand escort or statutory escort goes out, the she-sheng colonel, sima, clerks, soldiers, and warriors mount them, in order as attendant chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the grand or statutory cortège rolls out, archery colonels, adjutants, clerks, and troops ride these as the numbered attendant cars.

sentences.zh: 司南車，一名指南車，駕四馬，其下制如樓，三級；

translations.literal: The south-pointer chariot, one name is guide chariot, is hitched to four horses; its lower structure is like a tower of three tiers;
translations.idiomatic: The south-pointing carriage—also called the compass cart—draws four horses; its body stacks three gallery levels;

sentences.zh: 四角金龍銜羽葆；

translations.literal: At the four corners gold dragons hold feathered canopies;
translations.idiomatic: gold dragons at each corner grip feather-tasseled finials;

sentences.zh: 刻木為仙人，衣羽衣，立車上，車雖回運而手常南指。

translations.literal: Wood is carved as an immortal, clothed in a feather robe, standing on the chariot; though the chariot turns and wheels, the hand constantly points south.
translations.idiomatic: a carved immortal in feather cloak stands on deck and keeps an arm extended south no matter how the car swerves.

sentences.zh: 大駕出行，為先啟之乘。

translations.literal: When the grand escort goes out, it is the mount that opens the way ahead.
translations.idiomatic: It leads the whole imperial column.

sentences.zh: 記裏鼓車，駕四，形制如司南，其中有木人執棰向鼓，行一里則打一棰。

translations.literal: The mile-drum chariot is hitched to four horses; its shape is like the south-pointer; inside there is a wooden man holding a mallet toward the drum; when it goes one li it strikes one blow.
translations.idiomatic: The odometer drum car, four horses, resembles the guide carriage: a wooden figure inside beats a drum once every li traveled.

sentences.zh: 羊車，一名輦車，其上如軺，伏兔箱，漆畫輪軛。

translations.literal: The goat cart, one name is palanquin cart; its upper part is like a ya cart, with crouching-rabbit boxes, lacquered painted wheels and yoke.
translations.idiomatic: The “goat cart,” also called litter-style wagon, has a light upperworks like a patrol car, hare-shaped boxes, and lacquered wheels.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，護軍羊琇輒乘羊車，司隸劉毅糾劾其罪。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu’s time, the household guard Yang Xiu always rode a goat cart, and the metropolitan inspector Liu Yi impeached his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Wudi, Guard-general Yang Xiu habitually rode a goat-drawn cart until Liu Yi, metropolitan inspector, charged him for it.

sentences.zh: 畫輪車，駕牛，以彩漆畫輪轂，故名曰畫輪車。

translations.literal: The painted-wheel cart is drawn by oxen; because colored lacquer paints the hubs, it is therefore called the painted-wheel cart.
translations.idiomatic: Ox-drawn “painted-wheel” pleasure wagons take their name from their polychrome hub decoration.

sentences.zh: 上起四夾杖，左右開四望，綠油幢，硃絲絡，青交路，其上形制事事如輦，其下猶如犢車耳。

translations.literal: Above it raises four clamped posts; left and right open four outlooks; a green-oil canopy; cinnabar silk netting; green crossing bands; on top its form in every respect is like a palanquin, while below it is still like a calf cart.
translations.idiomatic: They sport corner posts, open viewing bays, green oilcloth canopies, red mesh, and green cross-straps—upperworks like an imperial litter, lower body like a humble ox calf cart.

sentences.zh: 古之貴者不乘牛車，漢武帝推恩之末，諸侯寡弱，貧者至乘牛車，其後稍見貴之。

translations.literal: In antiquity the noble did not ride ox carts; at the end of Emperor Wu of Han’s “extending grace” policy, the feudal lords were weak and poor, and the poor even rode ox carts; afterward they were gradually held in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Classical elites scorned ox carts, but after Han’s feudal houses withered under the “extending grace” edicts, impoverished nobles took to them; over time the fashion gained respectability.

sentences.zh: 自靈獻以來，天子至士遂以為常乘，至尊出朝堂舉哀乘之。

translations.literal: From Ling and Xian onward, from the Son of Heaven down to gentlemen they came to use them as regular conveyance; the most honored, when going out to the court hall to observe mourning, rode them.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Eastern Han emperors on, everyone up to the throne routinely used ox carts—even for sovereigns riding to court for obsequies.

sentences.zh: 屬車，一曰副車，一曰貳車，一曰左車。

translations.literal: Attendant chariots: one name is deputy chariot, one name is secondary chariot, one name is left chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Escort wagons are also termed deputy cars, second cars, or “left-side” cars in Han usage.

sentences.zh: 漢因秦制，大駕屬車八十一乘，行則中央左右分為行。

translations.literal: Han followed Qin regulations: the grand escort’s attendant chariots were eighty-one; when moving, the center, left, and right divided into lines.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept Qin’s rule of eighty-one attendant vehicles for the grand cortège, marching in center, left, and right files.

sentences.zh: 法駕屬車三十六乘。

translations.literal: The statutory escort’s attendant chariots were thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The mid-grade statutory escort used thirty-six follow cars.

sentences.zh: 最後車懸豹尾，豹尾以前比之省中。

translations.literal: On the hindmost chariot a leopard tail was suspended; before the leopard tail it was compared to being inside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The rearmost car flew a leopard-tail pennant; everything ahead of that marker counted as “within the palace” zone.

sentences.zh: 屬車皆皁蓋硃裏雲。

translations.literal: Attendant chariots all had black canopies with cinnabar inside and cloud pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Each escort wagon wore a black canopy lined red and painted with cloud motifs.

sentences.zh: 御衣車、御書車、禦軺車、禦藥車，皆駕牛。

translations.literal: Imperial wardrobe cart, imperial library cart, imperial patrol cart, imperial medicine cart—all were drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Luggage trains included robe, book, patrol, and medicine carts, all ox-drawn.

sentences.zh: 陽遂四望繐窗皁輪小形車，駕牛。

translations.literal: The yang-sui four-outlook cart with coarse-silk windows, black wheels, small form, drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Small black-wheeled “yang-sui” survey carts with gauze windows also used ox teams.

sentences.zh: 象車，漢鹵簿最在前。

translations.literal: The elephant cart was foremost in Han’s ceremonial escort.
translations.idiomatic: Han processions once led with an elephant car.

sentences.zh: 武帝太康中平吳後，南越獻馴象，詔作大車駕之，以載黃門鼓吹數十人，使越人騎之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu’s Taikang mid-period, after Wu was pacified, Southern Yue presented tame elephants; an edict ordered a great cart made to harness them, to carry several dozen yellow-gate musicians, with Yue men riding them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin conquered Wu in the Taikang era, Nanyue sent trained elephants; the court built huge wagons, loaded them with palace musicians, and seated southern handlers aloft.

sentences.zh: 元正大會，駕象入庭。

translations.literal: At the New Year’s great assembly, elephants were driven into the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: New Year audiences opened with elephants paraded into the palace yard.

sentences.zh: 中朝大駕鹵簿

translations.literal: The mid-court grand escort ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin capital grand cortège order (heading):

sentences.zh: 先象車，鼓吹一部，十三人，中道。

translations.literal: First the elephant cart, one band of musicians, thirteen men, in the center way.
translations.idiomatic: First comes the elephant wagon and a thirteen-man front band dead center.

sentences.zh: 次靜室令，駕一，中道。

translations.literal: Next the quiet-chamber commandant, driving one, in the center way.
translations.idiomatic: Then the private-chamber marshal, single car, center file.

sentences.zh: 式道候二人，駕一，分左右也。

translations.literal: Two road-form guards, driving one each, divide left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Two “road rite” inspectors follow in paired cars left and right.

sentences.zh: 次洛陽尉二人，騎，分左右。

translations.literal: Next two Luoyang constables, mounted, divide left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Next ride two Luoyang constables, split to the flanks.

sentences.zh: 次洛陽亭長九人，赤車，駕一，分三道，各吹正二人引。

translations.literal: Next nine Luoyang village headmen, red carts, driving one each, in three ways, each with two straight trumpeters leading.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Luoyang ward chiefs in red cars form three columns, each led by two trumpeters.

sentences.zh: 次洛陽令，皁車，駕一，中道。

translations.literal: Next the Luoyang magistrate, black cart, driving one, in the center way.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyang magistrate follows in a black official car down the center.

sentences.zh: 次河南中部掾，中道。

translations.literal: Next the Henan central department clerk, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Then Henan’s central-section adjutant, center lane.

sentences.zh: 河橋掾在左，功曹史在右，並駕一。

translations.literal: The river-bridge clerk is on the left, the merit clerk on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: River-bridge and merit clerks pair left and right, one car each.

sentences.zh: 次河南尹，駕駟，戟吏六人。

translations.literal: Next the Henan governor, driving four, six halberd clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan governor rides a four-horse carriage with six halberd attendants.

sentences.zh: 次河南主簿，駕一，中道。

translations.literal: Next the Henan chief clerk, driving one, center way.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk follows solo in the center.

sentences.zh: 次河南主記，駕一，中道。

translations.literal: Next the Henan chief recorder, driving one, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Then the chief recorder, same formation.

sentences.zh: 次司隸部河南從事，中道。

translations.literal: Next the metropolitan clerk of Henan under the provincial commandant, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Next comes the provincial inspector’s Henan staff officer, center.

sentences.zh: 都部從事居左，別駕從事居右，並駕一。

translations.literal: The capital-section clerk is on the left, the aide-de-camp clerk on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: Capital-section and aide clerks split left/right with one car apiece.

sentences.zh: 次司隸校尉，駕三，戟吏八人。

translations.literal: Next the provincial commandant, driving three, eight halberd clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial commandant uses a three-horse car and eight halberdiers.

sentences.zh: 次司隸主簿，駕一，中道。

translations.literal: Next the provincial chief clerk, driving one, center way.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk rides center behind him.

sentences.zh: 次司隸主記，駕一，中道。

translations.literal: Next the provincial chief recorder, driving one, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The chief recorder mirrors that slot.

sentences.zh: 次廷尉明法掾，中道。

translations.literal: Next the court’s law clerk under the commandant of justice, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The Court’s law-section adjutant advances down the middle.

sentences.zh: 五官掾居左，功曹史居右，並駕一。

translations.literal: The five-bureau clerk is on the left, the merit clerk on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: Five-bureau and merit clerks flank the justice team.

sentences.zh: 次廷尉卿，駕駟，戟吏六人。

translations.literal: Next the commandant of justice, driving four, six halberd clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant of justice rides four horses with six halberds.

sentences.zh: 次廷尉主簿、主記，並駕一，在左。

translations.literal: Next the court chief clerk and chief recorder, both driving one, on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Court chief clerk and recorder share a left-side car.

sentences.zh: 太僕引從如廷尉，在中。

translations.literal: The grand coachman’s escort follows like the commandant of justice, in the center.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coachman’s train matches the court layout, centered.

sentences.zh: 宗正引從如廷尉，在右。

translations.literal: The director of the imperial clan’s escort follows like the commandant of justice, on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial-clan director mirrors the court on the right.

sentences.zh: 次太常，駕駟，中道，戟吏六人。

translations.literal: Next the grand master of ceremonies, driving four, center way, six halberd clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The grand master of rites rides four-in-hand down the axis with six halberds.

sentences.zh: 太常外部掾居左，五官掾、功曹吏居右，並駕一。

translations.literal: The grand master of ceremonies’ external clerk is on the left, the five-bureau and merit clerks on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: His external and bureau clerks split the line behind him.

sentences.zh: 次光祿引從，中道。

translations.literal: Next the superintendent of the household escort, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The household superintendent’s escort fills the center next.

sentences.zh: 太常主簿、主記居左，衛尉引從居右，並駕一。

translations.literal: The grand master of ceremonies’ chief clerk and chief recorder are on the left, the commandant of the guard’s escort on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual clerks ride left while the guard commandant’s party rides right.

sentences.zh: 次太尉外督令史，駕一，中道。

translations.literal: Next the grand marshal’s external order clerk, driving one, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal’s exterior clerk follows solo center.

sentences.zh: 次西東賊倉戶等曹屬，並駕一，引從。

translations.literal: Next the western and eastern bandit and granary household bureau subordinates, all driving one each, leading and following.
translations.idiomatic: East and west “bandit” and granary bureau aides trail in single cars.

sentences.zh: 次太尉，駕駟，中道。

translations.literal: Next the grand marshal, driving four, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The grand marshal’s four-horse state coach anchors the center.

sentences.zh: 太尉主簿、舍人各一人，祭酒二人，並駕一，在左。

translations.literal: The grand marshal’s chief clerk and houseman one each, two libationers, all driving one, on the left.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk, chamberlain, and two libationers share left-side mounts.

sentences.zh: 次司徒引從，駕駟，中道。

translations.literal: Next the grand tutor’s escort, driving four, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The grand tutor follows with the same four-horse dignity.

sentences.zh: 次司空引從，駕駟，中道。

translations.literal: Next the grand minister of works’ escort, driving four, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of works repeats the pattern.

sentences.zh: 三公騎令史戟各八人，鼓吹各一部，七人。

translations.literal: The three excellencies’ mounted order clerks each have eight men with halberds, each one band of musicians, seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three dukes rates eight mounted clerks with halberds plus a seven-man band.

sentences.zh: 次中護軍，中道，駕駟。

translations.literal: Next the central guardian of the army, center way, driving four.
translations.idiomatic: The central army guardian rides four abreast on the axis.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿左右各二行，戟楯在外，弓矢在內，鼓吹一部，七人。

translations.literal: On each side of the escort two rows, halberd shields on the outside, bows and arrows on the inside, one band of musicians, seven men.
translations.idiomatic: His guard forms twin files: shields outward, archers inward, plus a seven-piece band per side.

sentences.zh: 次步兵校尉在左，長水校尉在右，並駕一。

translations.literal: Next the infantry colonel on the left, the long-shore colonel on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry and “long-shore” colonels pair left and right.

sentences.zh: 各鹵簿左右二行，戟楯在外，刀楯在內，鼓吹各一部，七人。

translations.literal: Each escort has left and right two rows, halberd shields on the outside, knife shields on the inside, each one band of musicians, seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Each colonel’s screen repeats halberd outer, blade-shield inner, with bands.

sentences.zh: 次射聲校尉在左，翊軍校尉在右，並駕一。

translations.literal: Next the archery-sound colonel on the left, the assisting-army colonel on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: Archery and “assisting army” colonels split the next rank.

sentences.zh: 各鹵簿左右各二行，戟楯在外，刀楯在內，鼓吹各一部，七人。

translations.literal: Each escort left and right each two rows, halberd shields on the outside, knife shields on the inside, each one band of musicians, seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Their formations mirror the previous pair.

sentences.zh: 次驍騎將軍在左，遊擊將軍在右，並駕一。

translations.literal: Next the fierce-cavalry general on the left, the roaming-strike general on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce cavalry and mobile-strike generals take the following slots.

sentences.zh: 皆鹵簿左右引各二行，戟楯在外，刀楯在內，鼓吹各一部，七人。

translations.literal: All escorts left and right each have two leading rows, halberd shields on the outside, knife shields on the inside, each one band of musicians, seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Each general’s escort again fields paired files with musicians.

sentences.zh: 騎隊，五在左，五在右，隊各五十匹，命中督二人分領左右。

translations.literal: Mounted squadrons: five on the left, five on the right; each squadron fifty horses, two strike colonels separately commanding left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Ten cavalry squadrons of fifty mounts each split five and five under two strike directors.

sentences.zh: 各有戟吏二人，麾幢獨揭，鼓在隊前。

translations.literal: Each has two halberd clerks; banners and pennons are raised singly; drums stand before the squadron.
translations.idiomatic: Every squadron posts halberd aides, lone streamers, and drums ahead.

sentences.zh: 次左將軍在左，前將軍在右，並駕一。

translations.literal: Next the general of the left on the left, the forward general on the right, both driving one each.
translations.idiomatic: Left and forward generals ride paired cars next.

sentences.zh: 皆鹵簿左右各二行，戟楯盾在外，刀楯在內，鼓吹各一部，七人。

translations.literal: All escorts left and right each two rows, halberd shields and shields on the outside, knife shields on the inside, each one band of musicians, seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Their guards add large shields outside, blade shields inside, plus bands.

sentences.zh: 次黃門麾騎，中道。

translations.literal: Next yellow-gate standard cavalry, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-gate mounted escorts tighten the center file.

sentences.zh: 次黃門前部鼓吹，左右各一部，十三人，駕駟。

translations.literal: Next yellow-gate front musicians, left and right each one band, thirteen men, driving four.
translations.idiomatic: Palace musicians split thirteen-player bands per side on four-horse wagons.

sentences.zh: 八校尉佐仗，左右各四行，外大戟楯，次九尺楯，次弓矢，次弩，並熊渠、佽飛督領之。

translations.literal: The eight colonels’ auxiliary halberds: left and right each four rows, great halberd shields on the outside, next nine-chi shields, next bows and arrows, next crossbows, all led by bear-channel and flying-strike colonels.
translations.idiomatic: Eight colonels’ guards stack four ranks apiece—great halberds, nine-foot shields, bows, then crossbows—under specialist colonels.

sentences.zh: 次司南車，駕駟，中道。

translations.literal: Next the south-pointer chariot, driving four, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The guide carriage returns to the axis, four horses.

sentences.zh: 護駕御史，騎，夾左右。

translations.literal: Attendant imperial censors, mounted, flanking left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial censors ride flanking the guide car.

sentences.zh: 次謁者僕射，駕駟，中道。

translations.literal: Next the supervisor of attendants, driving four, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies for audiences follows four-in-hand.

sentences.zh: 次御史中丞，駕一，中道。

translations.literal: Next the palace secretary supervisor, driving one, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial secretary rides a single state car center.

sentences.zh: 次武賁中郎將，騎，中道。

translations.literal: Next the household rapid guard general, mounted, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Next the rapid household guard general canters down the middle.

sentences.zh: 次九游車，中道，武剛車夾左右，並駕駟。

translations.literal: Next nine excursion chariots, center way, martial-hard chariots flanking left and right, both driving four.
translations.idiomatic: Nine “excursion” cars march center with armored “martial” wagons on both flanks.

sentences.zh: 次雲罕車，駕駟，中道。

translations.literal: Next the cloud-net chariot, driving four, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The yun-han car repeats, four horses center.

sentences.zh: 次闒戟車，駕駟，中道，長戟邪偃向後。

translations.literal: Next the halberd-rack chariot, driving four, center way, long halberds slanted backward.
translations.idiomatic: Halberd-rack cars follow, spears raked rearward.

sentences.zh: 次皮軒車，駕駟，中道。

translations.literal: Next the leather-screen chariot, driving four, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Leather-screen escort wagons close up the center.

sentences.zh: 次鸞旗車，中道，建華車分左右，並駕駟。

translations.literal: Next the luan-banner chariot, center way; splendor-blossom chariots divide left and right, both driving four.
translations.idiomatic: Luan-banner cars hold the axis while twin “splendid blossom” cars fan out.

sentences.zh: 次護駕尚書郎三人，都官郎中道，駕部在左，中兵在右，並騎。

translations.literal: Next three household guardian gentlemen of the masters of writing: the capital bureau gentleman center way, the equipage bureau on the left, the central army bureau on the right, all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Three ministerial escort riders—capital, equipage, and army bureaus—split center, left, and right.

sentences.zh: 又有護駕尚書一人，騎，督攝前後無常。

translations.literal: Moreover there is one household guardian gentleman of the masters of writing, mounted, supervising front and rear without fixity.
translations.idiomatic: A roving ministerial rider coordinates the whole segment.

sentences.zh: 次相風，中道。

translations.literal: Next the wind-reading vane, center way.
translations.idiomatic: A wind-reading device rolls up the center.

sentences.zh: 次司馬督，在前，中道。

translations.literal: Next the marshal supervisor, in front, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal supervisors advance at the head of the block.

sentences.zh: 左右各司馬史三人引仗，左右各六行，外大戟楯二行。

translations.literal: Left and right each three marshal clerks leading halberds; left and right each six rows; outside great halberd shields two rows.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal clerks lead six-deep files with great halberd shields outermost.

sentences.zh: 次九尺楯，次刀楯。

translations.literal: Next nine-chi shields, next knife shields.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-foot shields precede blade shields.

sentences.zh: 次弓矢，次弩。

translations.literal: Next bows and arrows, next crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Archers step before crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 次五時車，左右有遮列騎。

translations.literal: Next the five-season chariots; left and right have screening column cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Five-season cars ride with cordon cavalry on each side.

sentences.zh: 次典兵中郎，中道，督攝前卻無常。

translations.literal: Next the arms bureau gentleman, center way, supervising advance and retreat without fixity.
translations.idiomatic: An arms-bureau officer roves the line regulating pace.

sentences.zh: 左殿中御史，右殿中監，並騎。

translations.literal: Left palace censor, right palace intendant, both mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor left, palace intendant right, both ahorse.

sentences.zh: 次高蓋，中道，左罼，右罕。

translations.literal: Next tall canopy, center way, left bi net, right han net.
translations.idiomatic: High umbrellas march center flanked by bi and han feather screens.

sentences.zh: 次御史，中道，左右節郎各四人。

translations.literal: Next the censor, center way, left and right four section gentlemen each four men.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial censors advance on the axis, flanked by four section cadets per side.

sentences.zh: 次華蓋，中道。

translations.literal: Next the flowered canopy, center way.
translations.idiomatic: A great flowered umbrella follows on the center line.

sentences.zh: 次殿中司馬，中道。

translations.literal: Next the palace marshal, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The palace marshal’s detail rides dead center.

sentences.zh: 殿中都尉在左，殿中校尉在右，左右各四行。

translations.literal: The palace commandant is on the left, the palace colonel on the right; left and right each have four rows.
translations.idiomatic: Palace commandant left, palace colonel right, each with four ranks of guards.

sentences.zh: 細楯一行在弩內，又殿中司馬一行，殿中都尉一行，殿中校尉一行。

translations.literal: One row of small shields inside the crossbows, again one row of palace marshals, one row of palace commandants, one row of palace colonels.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the archers stands a file of light shields, then marshals, commandants, and colonels each in their own row.

sentences.zh: 次扌罡鼓，中道。

translations.literal: Next the pole drum (text reads 扌罡鼓), center way.
translations.idiomatic: Next roll the long-handled processional drums straight down the middle.

sentences.zh: 次金根車，駕六馬，中道。

translations.literal: Next the metal-root chariot, hitched to six horses, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s six-horse metal-root car occupies the axis.

sentences.zh: 太僕卿禦，大將軍參乘。

translations.literal: The grand coachman drives; the grand general is riding companion.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coachman holds the reins while the grand general sits beside him.

sentences.zh: 左右又各增三行，為九行。

translations.literal: Left and right each add three rows, making nine rows.
translations.idiomatic: Three extra files join each flank, widening the screen to nine deep.

sentences.zh: 司馬史九人，引大戟楯二行，九尺楯一行，刀楯一行，由基一行，細弩一行，跡禽一行，椎斧一行，力人刀楯一行。

translations.literal: Nine marshal clerks lead two rows of great halberd shields, one row of nine-chi shields, one row of knife shields, one row of Youji archers, one row of fine crossbows, one row of game trackers, one row of maul-axes, one row of strong men with knife shields.
translations.idiomatic: Nine adjutants shepherd stacked ranks: great halberds, nine-foot shields, blade shields, elite Youji bowmen, light crossbows, tracker squads, axe parties, and heavy infantry with shields.

sentences.zh: 連細楯，殿中司馬，殿中都尉，殿中校尉，為左右各十二行。

translations.literal: Linking small shields, palace marshals, palace commandants, palace colonels, for left and right each twelve rows.
translations.idiomatic: Light shields tie the formation to palace marshals, commandants, and colonels—twelve files on each side.

sentences.zh: 金根車建青旂十二。

translations.literal: The metal-root chariot raises twelve green banners.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial car flies twelve green streamers.

sentences.zh: 左將軍騎在左，右將軍騎在右，殿中將軍持鑿腦斧夾車，車後衣書主職步從，六行，合左右三十二行。

translations.literal: The general of the left rides on the left, the general of the right on the right; palace generals hold notched battle-axes hugging the car; behind the car wardrobe and library clerks walk in attendance, six rows; together left and right make thirty-two rows.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right generals pace the flanks while palace generals brace the car with axe guards; wardrobe and archive clerks trail on foot in six columns—thirty-two ranks in all.

sentences.zh: 次曲華蓋，中道。

translations.literal: Next the curved flowered canopy, center way.
translations.idiomatic: A domed flowered umbrella closes over the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 侍中、散騎常侍、黃門侍郎並騎，分左右。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary, cavalry attendant-in-ordinary, and yellow-gate gentleman riders all mounted, dividing left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Palace intimates—attendants-in-ordinary and yellow-gate gentlemen—split left and right on horseback.

sentences.zh: 次黃鉞車，駕一，在左，禦麾騎在右。

translations.literal: Next the yellow battle-axe chariot, driving one, on the left; the imperial standard cavalry on the right.
translations.idiomatic: A single car bears the gilded axe leftward while standard-bearing riders hold the right.

sentences.zh: 次相風，中道。

translations.literal: Next the wind-reading vane, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Another wind vane marks the center.

sentences.zh: 次中書監騎左，秘書監騎右。

translations.literal: Next the secretariat director rides left, the palace library director rides right.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat and palace library directors bracket the column.

sentences.zh: 次殿中御史騎左，殿中監騎右。

translations.literal: Next the palace censor rides left, the palace intendant rides right.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor to the left, palace intendant to the right.

sentences.zh: 次五牛旗，赤青在左，黃在中，白黑在右。

translations.literal: Next the five-ox banner, red and green on the left, yellow in the center, white and black on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The five-ox standard returns with its fixed color positions.

sentences.zh: 次大輦，中道。

translations.literal: Next the great palanquin, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The great imperial litter follows on the axis.

sentences.zh: 太官令丞在左，太醫令丞在右。

translations.literal: The grand provisioner director and aide are on the left, the grand physician director and aide on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Court caterers ride left, court physicians right of the litter.

sentences.zh: 次金根車，駕駟，不建旗。

translations.literal: Next the metal-root chariot, driving four, not raising banners.
translations.idiomatic: A second metal-root car, four horses, flies no tall standards.

sentences.zh: 次青立車，次青安車，次赤立車，次赤安車，次黃立車，次黃安車，次白立車，次白安車，次黑立車，次黑安車，合十乘，並駕駟。

translations.literal: Next green standing chariot, next green peace chariot, next red standing, next red peace, next yellow standing, next yellow peace, next white standing, next white peace, next black standing, next black peace—ten chariots in all—all driving four.
translations.idiomatic: Ten five-season cars follow in order—green, red, yellow, white, and black, each in standing and seated styles—all four-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 建旗十二，如車色。

translations.literal: Twelve banners are raised, matching the chariot colors.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pennons are dyed to match their cars.

sentences.zh: 立車正豎旗，安東邪拖之。

translations.literal: Standing chariots set the banner straight upright; peace chariots (text reads 安東) slant and trail them.
translations.idiomatic: Standing cars fly vertical poles; seated cars trail their banners at an angle.

sentences.zh: 次蹋豬車，駕駟，中道，無旗。

translations.literal: Next the pig-tread chariot, driving four, center way, without banners.
translations.idiomatic: The low hunt wagon (pig-tread style) follows four-in-hand, unbannered.

sentences.zh: 次耕根車，駕駟，中道，赤旗十二，熊渠督左，佽飛督右。

translations.literal: Next the ploughing-root chariot, driving four, center way, twelve red banners, bear-channel colonel on the left, flying-strike colonel on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The ploughing car rides four abreast with twelve scarlet streamers, flanked by bear-channel and flying-strike colonels.

sentences.zh: 次禦軺車，次禦四望車，次御衣車，次御書車，次禦藥車，並駕牛，中道。

translations.literal: Next the imperial patrol cart, next the imperial four-outlook cart, next the imperial wardrobe cart, next the imperial library cart, next the imperial medicine cart—all drawn by oxen, center way.
translations.idiomatic: Ox-drawn imperial service wagons—patrol, survey, wardrobe, archive, and pharmacy—string along the center.

sentences.zh: 次尚書令在左，尚書僕射在右，又尚書郎六人，分次左右，並駕。

translations.literal: Next the masters of writing director on the left, the vice director on the right, again six masters of writing gentlemen, dividing in order left and right, all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: The minister and vice-minister of the masters of writing lead, with six secretaries split to either flank, all riding.

sentences.zh: 又治書侍御史二人，分左右，又侍御史二人，分次左右，又蘭台令史分次左右，並騎。

translations.literal: Again two supervising secretaries attending censors divide left and right; again two attending censors divide in order left and right; again orchid terrace clerks divide in order left and right, all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censors, attending censors, and orchid-terrace clerks mirror the same left-right pairing on horseback.

sentences.zh: 次豹尾車，駕一。

translations.literal: Next the leopard-tail chariot, driving one.
translations.idiomatic: The leopard-tail escort car rides alone.

sentences.zh: 自豹尾車後而鹵簿盡矣。

translations.literal: From behind the leopard-tail chariot the ceremonial guard is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the leopard-tail wagon the formal cortège ends.

sentences.zh: 但以神弩二十張夾道，至後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: But twenty divine crossbows line the road on both sides, reaching to the rear musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Yet twenty heavy crossbows still line the route rearward to the trailing bands.

sentences.zh: 其五張神弩置一將，左右各二將。

translations.literal: For every five divine crossbows one commander is posted; left and right each have two commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Each five-piece battery has its own captain, two captains to a side.

sentences.zh: 次輕車二十乘，左右分駕。

translations.literal: Next twenty light chariots, left and right separately driving.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty light wagons split evenly to the flanks.

sentences.zh: 次流蘇馬六十匹。

translations.literal: Next sixty tassel horses.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty horses with silk tassels follow.

sentences.zh: 次金鉞車，駕三，中道。

translations.literal: Next the golden battle-axe chariot, driving three, center way.
translations.idiomatic: A three-horse gilded-axe car rides center.

sentences.zh: 左右護駕尚書郎並令史，並騎，各一人。

translations.literal: Left and right household guardian masters of writing gentlemen and clerks, all mounted, each one man.
translations.idiomatic: Ministerial escort riders and clerks bracket the axe car, one rider each side.

sentences.zh: 次金鉦車，駕三，中道。

translations.literal: Next the golden gong chariot, driving three, center way.
translations.idiomatic: A three-horse gilded gong wagon comes next on the axis.

sentences.zh: 左右護駕侍御史並令史等，並騎，各一人。

translations.literal: Left and right household guardian attending censors and clerks, all mounted, each one man.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial escorts and clerks mirror the gong car left and right.

sentences.zh: 次黃門後部鼓吹，左右各十三人。

translations.literal: Next yellow-gate rear musicians, left and right thirteen men each.
translations.idiomatic: Rear palace bands post thirteen players per flank.

sentences.zh: 次戟鼓車，駕牛，二乘，分左右。

translations.literal: Next halberd-drum carts, drawn by oxen, two chariots, dividing left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Two ox-drawn drum-and-halberd wagons split to the sides.

sentences.zh: 次左大鴻臚外部掾，右五官掾、功曹史，並駕。

translations.literal: Next the left grand herald external clerk, the right five-bureau and merit clerks, all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand herald aides ride left; five-bureau and merit clerks right.

sentences.zh: 次大鴻臚，駕駟，鉞吏六人。

translations.literal: Next the grand herald, driving four, six axe clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The grand herald of guests rides four-in-hand with six axemen.

sentences.zh: 次大司農引從，中道，左大鴻臚主簿、主記，右少府引從。

translations.literal: Next the grand minister of agriculture leading followers, center way; left grand herald chief clerk and chief recorder, right minister of the less palace leading followers.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of finance centers the block while herald and household ministers trail their staffs on either side.

sentences.zh: 次三卿，並騎，吏四人，鈴下二人，執馬鞭辟車六人，執方扇羽林十人，硃衣。

translations.literal: Next the three ministers, all mounted, four clerks, two bell attendants, six men holding horse whips clearing the road, ten imperial guard men with square fans, cinnabar robes.
translations.idiomatic: The three senior ministers ride with clerks, bell pages, road-clearers with whips, ten feather-fan guards in red.

sentences.zh: 次領軍將軍，中道。

translations.literal: Next the commanding general of the army, center way.
translations.idiomatic: The commanding general closes the center file.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿左右各二行，九尺楯在外，弓矢在內，鼓吹如護軍。

translations.literal: The escort left and right each two rows, nine-chi shields on the outside, bows and arrows on the inside, musicians like the guardian of the army.
translations.idiomatic: His screen repeats the army-guard pattern—nine-foot shields out, archers in, matched bands.

sentences.zh: 次後軍將軍在左，右將軍在右，各鹵簿鼓吹如左軍、前軍。

translations.literal: Next the rear army general on the left, the right general on the right; each escort and musicians like the left army and forward army.
translations.idiomatic: Rear and right army generals mirror the left and forward army formations.

sentences.zh: 次越騎校尉在左，屯騎校尉在右，各鹵簿鼓吹如步兵、射聲。

translations.literal: Next the colonel of Yue cavalry on the left, the colonel of encampment cavalry on the right; each escort and musicians like the infantry and archery-sound colonels.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and encampment cavalry colonels copy the infantry and archery colonels’ layouts.

sentences.zh: 次領護驍騎、游軍校尉，皆騎，吏四人，乘馬夾道，都督兵曹各一人，乘馬在中。

translations.literal: Next the colonels leading and guarding fierce cavalry and roaming army, all mounted, four clerks, riding horses lining the road, army and bureau overseers each one man riding in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Colonels of fierce and roaming guards ride with clerks lining the avenue while bureau overseers hold the middle.

sentences.zh: 騎將軍四人，騎校、鞉角、金鼓、鈴下、信幡、軍校並駕一。

translations.literal: Four mounted generals, mounted colonels, hand-drums, horns, metal drums, bell attendants, signal banners, and army clerks each drive one.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted generals and colonels share cars with drummers, horn players, gongs, pages, signal flags, and adjutants.

sentences.zh: 功曹吏、主簿並騎從。

translations.literal: Merit clerks and chief clerks all mounted in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Chief and merit clerks follow on horseback.

sentences.zh: 扇幢麾各一騎，鼓吹一部，七騎。

translations.literal: Fan, canopy, and banner each one rider; one band of musicians, seven riders.
translations.idiomatic: Each fan, canopy, and standard gets a rider; bands number seven horsemen.

sentences.zh: 次領護軍，加大車斧，五官掾騎從。

translations.literal: Next the commanding guardian of the army, adding great cart axes, five-bureau clerks mounted in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The commanding guardian rides with great cart axes and five-bureau escorts.

sentences.zh: 次騎十隊，隊各五十匹。

translations.literal: Next ten cavalry squadrons, each squadron fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Ten cavalry troops of fifty mounts apiece follow.

sentences.zh: 將一人，持幢一人，鞉一人，並騎在前，督戰伯長各一人，並騎在後，羽林騎督、幽州突騎督分領之。

translations.literal: One commander, one man holding a canopy, one drummer, all mounted in front; battle overseers and squad chiefs each one man, all mounted behind; feather-forest cavalry colonel and Youzhou shock cavalry colonel divide command of them.
translations.idiomatic: Each troop fronts a commander, standard bearer, and drummer, with overseers and chiefs riding rear; forest cavalry and Youzhou shock colonels split leadership.

sentences.zh: 郎簿十隊，隊各五十人。

translations.literal: Gentleman guard ten squads, each squad fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: Ten fifty-man gentleman guard companies march behind.

sentences.zh: 絳袍將一人，騎、鞉各一人，在前，督戰伯長各一人，步，在後。

translations.literal: One crimson-robed commander, mounted, one drummer in front, battle overseers and squad chiefs each one man on foot behind.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson-clad commanders lead mounted drummers while foot overseers bring up the rear.

sentences.zh: 騎皆持槊。

translations.literal: The cavalry all hold lances.
translations.idiomatic: Every rider carries a lance.

sentences.zh: 次大戟一隊，九尺楯一隊，刀楯一隊，弓一隊，弩一隊，隊各五十人。

translations.literal: Next one squad of great halberds, one squad of nine-chi shields, one squad of knife shields, one squad of bows, one squad of crossbows; each squad fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry blocks follow: halberdiers, nine-foot shieldmen, blade shields, bowmen, and crossbowmen—fifty each.

sentences.zh: 黑袴褶將一人，騎校、鞉角各一人，步，在前，督戰伯長各一人，步，在後。

translations.literal: One black-trouser commander, mounted colonel and horn each one man on foot in front, battle overseers and squad chiefs each one man on foot behind.
translations.idiomatic: Black-uniform commanders head each block with mounted colonels and horn players ahead, overseers afoot behind.

sentences.zh: 金顏督將並領之。

translations.literal: The gold-visored colonels jointly lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector colonels (gold-visored officers) jointly command these files.

sentences.zh: 皇太子安車，駕三，左右騑。

translations.literal: The heir apparent’s peace chariot is hitched to three horses, left and right trace horses.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince’s seated carriage uses three horses with outriggers.

sentences.zh: 硃班輪，倚獸較，伏鹿軾。

translations.literal: Vermillion-spotted wheels, leaning bars with crouching beasts, shield-grip with crouching deer.
translations.idiomatic: Vermillion-flecked wheels, animal-carved leaning rails, and a deer motif on the front shield.

sentences.zh: 九旒，畫降龍。

translations.literal: Nine tassels, painting descending dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Nine streamers bear painted descending dragons.

sentences.zh: 青蓋，金華蚤二十八枚。

translations.literal: Green canopy, golden splendor nails twenty-eight pieces.
translations.idiomatic: A green canopy carries twenty-eight gilded rib caps.

sentences.zh: 黑文畫轓，文輈，黃金塗五采。

translations.literal: Black patterns paint the fenders, patterned shaft, five colors overlaid with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Black scrollwork trims the fenders; the pole is patterned and gilded in five colors.

sentences.zh: 亦謂之鸞路。

translations.literal: It is also called the luan lu.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers also call it the heir’s “luan” carriage.

sentences.zh: 非法駕則乘畫輪車，上開四望，綠油幢，硃絲繩絡，兩箱裏飾以金錦，黃金塗五采。

translations.literal: If not the statutory ride, then he rides the painted-wheel cart, opening four outlooks above, green-oil canopy, cinnabar silk netting, both side boxes inside ornamented with gold brocade, gold overlaid with five colors.
