translations.idiomatic: On informal outings he uses the painted-wheel survey car—open galleries, green canopy, red mesh, gold brocade lining the boxes, polychrome gilding.

sentences.zh: 其副車三乘，形制如所乘，但不畫輪耳。

translations.literal: His deputy chariots are three; the form is like what he rides, but they do not paint the wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Three escort cars match his train except their wheels stay unpainted.

sentences.zh: 王青蓋車，皇孫綠蓋車，並駕三，左右騑。

translations.literal: Princes’ green-canopy chariot, imperial grandsons’ green-canopy chariot, both hitched to three, left and right trace horses.
translations.idiomatic: Princes ride green-canopy cars; imperial grandsons use a greener shade—both three-horse with outriggers.

sentences.zh: 雲母車，以雲母飾犢車。

translations.literal: The mica chariot uses mica to ornament the calf cart.
translations.idiomatic: The “mica wagon” plates a calf cart with mica panels.

sentences.zh: 臣下不得乘，以賜王公耳。

translations.literal: Subordinates may not ride it; it is conferred on dukes and princes only.
translations.idiomatic: Only kings and dukes receive this honor; lower ranks may not use it.

sentences.zh: 皁輪車，駕四牛，形制猶如犢車，但皁漆輪轂，上加青油幢，硃絲繩絡。

translations.literal: The black-wheel chariot is drawn by four oxen; its form is still like a calf cart, but wheels and hubs are lacquered black, with green-oil canopy above and cinnabar silk netting.
translations.idiomatic: The black-wheel ox cart resembles a calf car but for jet-black wheels, green oilcloth roof, and red mesh.

sentences.zh: 諸王三公有勳德者特加之。

translations.literal: Princes and three dukes who have merit and virtue are specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne awards it only to meritorious princes and three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 位至公或四望、三望、夾望車。

translations.literal: Those who reach duke rank may receive four-outlook, three-outlook, or flanked-outlook chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes may graduate to multi-outlook survey wagons as rank allows.

sentences.zh: 油幢車，駕牛，形制如皁輪，但不漆轂耳。

translations.literal: The oil-canopy chariot is drawn by oxen; its form is like the black-wheel, but it does not lacquer the hubs.
translations.idiomatic: Oil-canopy ox carts match black-wheel style except the hubs stay plain.

sentences.zh: 王公大臣有勳德者特給之。

translations.literal: Dukes, princes, and great ministers who have merit and virtue are specially given them.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious dukes and senior ministers alone receive these vehicles.

sentences.zh: 通幰車，駕牛，猶如今犢車制，但舉其幰通覆車上也。

translations.literal: The open-curtain chariot is drawn by oxen; it is still like today’s calf cart system, but it lifts its curtain to cover the whole car above.
translations.idiomatic: The “through-curtain” ox cart works like a modern calf car but drapes a continuous awning over the top.

sentences.zh: 諸王三公並乘之。

translations.literal: The various princes and three dukes all ride them.
translations.idiomatic: All princes and three excellencies may use this type.

sentences.zh: 諸公給朝車駕四、安車黑耳駕三各一乘，皁輪犢車各一乘。

translations.literal: The various dukes are given court chariots driving four, peace chariots with black ears driving three, one each, and black-wheel calf carts one each.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes receive a four-horse court car, a three-horse black-eared peace car, and a black-wheel calf cart apiece.

sentences.zh: 自祭酒掾屬以下及令史，皆皁零，辟朝服。

translations.literal: From libationer clerks down to record clerks, all ride black-covered mounts (text reads 皁零) and observe court dress.
translations.idiomatic: From libationer aides down to archivists everyone rides black-canopied carts and wears full court robes.

sentences.zh: 其武官公又別給大車。

translations.literal: Martial office dukes are separately given great carts.
translations.idiomatic: Generals who hold ducal rank also receive heavy supply wagons.

sentences.zh: 特進及車騎將軍驃騎將軍以下諸大將軍不開府非持節都督者，給安車黑耳駕二，軺車施耳後戶一乘。

translations.literal: For fully eminent nobles and grand generals of chariot and cavalry, swift cavalry, and below who do not open offices and are not area commanders with credentials, they are given peace chariots with black ears driving two, and one patrol cart with ears and rear door.
translations.idiomatic: Senior nobles and full generals short of independent commands get two-horse peace cars plus a single patrol wagon with ear screens and a rear door.

sentences.zh: 三公、九卿、中二千石、二千石、河南尹、謁者僕射、郊廟明堂法出，皆大車立乘，駕駟。

translations.literal: The three excellencies, nine ministers, those at two thousand piculs full and regular, the Henan governor, the supervisor of attendants, for statutory outings to suburban altars, bright hall, and law processions, all use great carts standing to ride, driving four.
translations.idiomatic: For state rituals the three dukes, nine ministers, full two-thousand-bushel officials, the Luoyang governor, and the master of ceremonies ride standing in four-horse state wagons.

sentences.zh: 前後導從大車駕二，右騑。

translations.literal: Front and rear guides and followers use great carts driving two, right trace horse.
translations.idiomatic: Their escorts use two-horse wagons with a right outrigger.

sentences.zh: 他出乘安車。

translations.literal: For other outings they ride peace chariots.
translations.idiomatic: On ordinary business they switch to seated carriages.

sentences.zh: 其去位致仕告老，賜安車駟馬。

translations.literal: Those who leave office, retire, or announce old age are granted peace chariots and four horses.
translations.idiomatic: Retiring officials receive a honorific four-horse peace car.

sentences.zh: 郡縣公侯，安車駕二，右騑。

translations.literal: District, county, dukes, and marquises: peace chariot driving two, right trace horse.
translations.idiomatic: County-level nobles ride two-horse peace cars with a right trace.

sentences.zh: 皆硃班輪，倚鹿較，伏熊軾，黑輜，皁繒蓋。

translations.literal: All have vermillion-spotted wheels, leaning bars with crouching deer, shield-grip with crouching bear, black carriage box, black silk canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Their cars share vermilion-flecked wheels, deer-carved rails, bear motifs on the shield, black coachwork, and sable canopies.

sentences.zh: 公旗旂八旒，侯七旒，卿五旒，皆畫降龍。

translations.literal: Dukes’ banners and flags have eight tassels, marquises seven, ministers five, all painting descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Ducal standards carry eight streamers, marquis seven, minister five—each with descending dragons.

sentences.zh: 中二千石、二千石，皆皁蓋，硃兩轓，銅五采，駕二。

translations.literal: Those at two thousand piculs full and regular, and two thousand piculs, all have black canopies, cinnabar two fenders, bronze five colors, driving two.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thousand-bushel officials use black tops, red paired fenders, bronze five-color trim, and two-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 中二千石以上，右騑。

translations.literal: Those above full two thousand piculs have the right trace horse.
translations.idiomatic: Full two-thousand ranks add a right-side outrigger.

sentences.zh: 千石、六百石，硃左轓。

translations.literal: One thousand piculs and six hundred piculs have cinnabar left fender.
translations.idiomatic: Lower salaried ranks mark only the left fender in vermilion.

sentences.zh: 車轓長六尺，下屈廣八寸，上業廣尺二寸，九丈，十二初，後謙一寸，若月初生，示不敢自滿也。

translations.literal: The chariot fender is six chi long; the lower bend is eight cun wide; the upper edge is one chi two cun wide; nine zhang, twelve beginnings; the rear modest one cun, like the new moon’s first crescent, showing not daring to be self-full.
translations.idiomatic: Fenders measure six chi along the curve, eight cun at the bend, twelve cun at the crown, with nine-zhang silk and twelve pleats; the rear tip cuts inward one cun like a new moon to symbolize modesty.

sentences.zh: 王公之世子攝命理國者，安車，駕三，旗旂七旒，其封侯之世子五旒。

translations.literal: Heir sons of kings and dukes who hold office and administer the state have peace chariots driving three, banners and flags with seven tassels; heir sons enfeoffed as marquises have five tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Princely heirs who govern draw three-horse peace cars with seven streamers; marquis’ heirs use five.

sentences.zh: 太康四年，制：「依漢故事，給九卿朝車駕四及安車各一乘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taikang, the regulation said: “According to Han precedent, give the nine ministers court chariots driving four and peace chariots one each.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang year four issued: “Follow Han practice—grant each of the nine ministers a four-horse court wagon plus one peace car.”

sentences.zh: 」八年，詔：「諸尚書軍校加侍中常侍者，皆給傳事乘軺車，給劍，得入殿省中，與侍臣升降相隨。」

translations.literal: ” In the eighth year, an edict said: “For various masters of writing army clerks who add attendant-in-ordinary or cavalry attendant-in-ordinary, all give courier duty riding patrol carts, give swords, allowing entry to palace halls, ascending and descending with attendant officials.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Eight years later an edict added: “Secretariat army aides who also hold attendant-in-ordinary titles receive fast patrol cars and swords so they may enter palace corridors and move with the inner court.”

sentences.zh: 大使車，立乘，駕四，赤帷裳，騶騎導從。

translations.literal: The great envoy chariot is ridden standing, hitched to four, red curtains and skirts, outriders clearing the way.
translations.idiomatic: Senior envoys use tall four-horse cars with crimson drapery and mounted escorts opening the road.

sentences.zh: 舊公卿二千石郊廟上陵從駕，乘大使車，他出乘安車也。

translations.literal: Formerly dukes and ministers at two thousand piculs for suburban altars, imperial tombs, and following the chariot rode the great envoy chariot; for other outings they rode peace chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Han rules had two-thousand-bushel nobles stand in the great envoy wagon for state sacrifices and tomb rites, then switch to seated cars elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 小使車，不立乘，駕四，輕車之流也。

translations.literal: The small envoy chariot is not ridden standing; it is hitched to four; it is of the light chariot class.
translations.idiomatic: The “small envoy” model is a seated four-horse light carriage.

sentences.zh: 蘭輿皆硃，赤轂，赤屏泥，白蓋，赤帷裳，從騶騎四十人。

translations.literal: Orchid carts are all vermillion, red hubs, red mud-screens, white canopy, red curtains and skirts; forty mounted escorts follow.
translations.idiomatic: “Orchid” escort wagons are scarlet with red wheels, white tops, red hangings, and forty outriders.

sentences.zh: 又別有小使車，赤轂皁蓋，追捕考案有所執取者之所乘也。

translations.literal: Moreover there is separately a small envoy chariot, red hubs and black canopy, for those who pursue, capture, investigate, and take persons into custody to ride.
translations.idiomatic: A darker variant with black canopy serves police inspectors on arrests and inquests.

sentences.zh: 凡諸使車皆硃班輪，赤衡軛。

translations.literal: In general the various envoy chariots all have vermillion-spotted wheels and red crossbar and yoke.
translations.idiomatic: All official messenger cars share vermilion-flecked wheels and red yoke hardware.

sentences.zh: 追鋒車，去小平蓋，加通幰，如軺車，駕二。

translations.literal: The swift-fringe chariot removes the small flat canopy, adds a through-curtain, like a patrol cart, hitched to two.
translations.idiomatic: “Swift-fringe” couriers strip the small roof for a full awning like a patrol car and use two horses.

sentences.zh: 追鋒之名，蓋取其迅速也，施於戎陣之間，是為傳乘。

translations.literal: The name swift-fringe probably takes from its speed; applied within battle arrays, this is called relay riding.
translations.idiomatic: The name signals speed; on campaign it serves as the dash relay vehicle.

sentences.zh: 軺車，古之時軍車也。

translations.literal: The patrol cart was in antiquity the army chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol cars descend from Han military runabouts.

sentences.zh: 一馬曰軺車，二馬曰軺傳。

translations.literal: One horse is called patrol cart; two horses is called patrol relay.
translations.idiomatic: One-horse models are “patrol cars”; paired teams are “patrol relays.”

sentences.zh: 漢世貴輜軿而賤軺車，魏晉重軺車而賤輜軿。

translations.literal: Han generations esteemed enclosed wagons and disdained patrol carts; Wei and Jin esteemed patrol carts and disdained enclosed wagons.
translations.idiomatic: Han fashion favored closed sedans; Wei–Jin reversed the prestige to light patrol cars.

sentences.zh: 三品將軍以上、尚書令軺車黑耳有後戶，僕射但有後戶無耳，並皁輪。

translations.literal: For third-rank generals and above and the masters of writing director, the patrol cart has black ears and a rear door; the vice director has only a rear door without ears; both have black wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Generals of third rank and the minister of state get black-eared patrol cars with back doors; vice ministers lose the “ears” but keep the rear hatch—all on black wheels.

sentences.zh: 尚書及四品將軍則無後戶，漆轂輪。

translations.literal: For masters of writing and fourth-rank generals there is no rear door; hubs and wheels are lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank officers ride simpler patrol wagons without rear doors but lacquered hubs.

sentences.zh: 其中書監令如僕射，侍中、黃門、散騎，初拜及謁陵廟，亦得乘之。

translations.literal: For secretariat director and vice like the vice director, attendant-in-ordinary, yellow gate, and cavalry attendant-in-ordinary, on first appointment and when visiting imperial tombs they also may ride them.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat directors, attendants-in-ordinary, and yellow-gate nobles may use these cars for first appointments and tomb pilgrimages.

sentences.zh: 皇太后、皇后法駕，乘重翟羽蓋金根車，駕青輅，青帷裳，雲畫轅，黃金塗五采，蓋爪施金華，駕三，左右騑。

translations.literal: For the empress dowager and empress statutory escort, they ride the layered kingfisher-feather canopy metal-root chariot, hitched to green lu, green curtains and skirts, cloud-painted shaft, gold overlaid with five colors; canopy claws apply golden splendor; hitched to three, left and right trace horses.
translations.idiomatic: The two highest ladies ride stacked kingfisher canopies on metal-root frames, green ritual cars, cloud-painted poles, gilded fittings, three gray horses with outriggers.

sentences.zh: 其廟見小駕，則乘紫罽軿車，雲畫輈，黃金塗五采，駕三。

translations.literal: For temple audiences with the small escort, they ride the purple felt enclosed wagon, cloud-painted pole, gold overlaid with five colors, hitched to three.
translations.idiomatic: For lesser ritual they switch to purple felt sedans with three-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 非法駕則皇太后乘輦，皇后乘畫輪車。

translations.literal: If not the statutory ride, then the empress dowager rides a palanquin and the empress rides a painted-wheel chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Informal outings put the dowager in a litter and the empress in a painted-wheel survey car.

sentences.zh: 皇后先蠶，乘油畫雲母安車，駕六騩馬；

translations.literal: For the empress’s first silkworm rite she rides an oil-painted mica peace chariot, hitched to six gui horses;
translations.idiomatic: The silkworm ceremony uses an oil-painted mica peace car with six dapple-gray mounts;

sentences.zh: 騩，淺黑色。

translations.literal: Gui means light black.
translations.idiomatic: “Gui” denotes blue-black horses.

sentences.zh: 油畫兩轅安車，駕五騩馬，為副。

translations.literal: An oil-painted two-shaft peace chariot, hitched to five gui horses, serves as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: A five-horse twin-shaft duplicate trails as escort.

sentences.zh: 又，金薄石山軿、紫絳罽軿車，皆駕三騩馬，為副。

translations.literal: Moreover, thin-gold stone-mountain enclosed wagons and purple-red felt enclosed wagons are all hitched to three gui horses as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-foil “stone mountain” sedans and purple felt cars follow with three-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 女旄頭十二人，持棨戟二人，共載安車，儷駕。

translations.literal: Twelve women yak-tail guards, two holding halberds, together load a peace chariot, paired hitch.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve female yak-tail runners pair-drive a support peace car with two halberdiers aboard.

sentences.zh: 女尚輦十二人，乘輜車，儷駕。

translations.literal: Twelve women palanquin attendants ride enclosed wagons, paired hitch.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve litter maids ride closed wagons in paired teams.

sentences.zh: 女長禦八人，乘安車，儷駕。

translations.literal: Eight women chief drivers ride peace chariots, paired hitch.
translations.idiomatic: Eight senior maids drive their own peace cars, paired.

sentences.zh: 三夫人油軿車，駕兩馬，左騑。

translations.literal: The three consorts ride oil enclosed wagons, hitched to two horses, left trace horse.
translations.idiomatic: The three chief consorts use oilcloth sedans, two horses plus a left outrigger.

sentences.zh: 其貴人駕節畫輈。

translations.literal: The honored ladies drive festival-painted poles.
translations.idiomatic: Lower-ranked noble ladies get simpler pole decoration.

sentences.zh: 三夫人助蠶，乘青交路，安車，駕三，皆以紫絳罽軿車。

translations.literal: The three consorts assisting at silkworm rite ride green crossing-band peace chariots, hitched to three, all using purple-red felt enclosed wagons.
translations.idiomatic: At the consorts’ silkworm aid they take green-banded three-horse peace cars with purple felt duplicates.

sentences.zh: 九嬪世婦乘軿車，駕三。

translations.literal: The nine concubines and noble wives ride enclosed wagons, hitched to three.
translations.idiomatic: Nine concubines and chief wives ride three-horse sedans.

sentences.zh: 長公主赤罽軿車，駕兩馬。

translations.literal: The senior princess rides a red felt enclosed wagon, hitched to two horses.
translations.idiomatic: Senior princesses use crimson felt two-horse sedans.

sentences.zh: 公主、王太妃、王妃，皆油軿車，駕兩馬，右騑。

translations.literal: Princesses, royal grand consorts, and princes’ consorts all ride oil enclosed wagons, hitched to two horses, right trace horse.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princesses and princely consorts take oilcloth sedans with two horses and a right trace.

sentences.zh: 公主油畫安車，駕三，青交路，以紫絳罽軿車駕三為副，王太妃、三夫人亦如之。

translations.literal: Princesses’ oil-painted peace chariots are hitched to three with green crossing bands, using purple-red felt enclosed wagons hitched to three as deputies; royal grand consorts and the three consorts are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses’ formal three-horse cars match grand consorts’ and chief consorts’ purple felt escorts.

sentences.zh: 公主助蠶，乘油畫安車，駕三。

translations.literal: Princesses assisting at silkworm ride oil-painted peace chariots, hitched to three.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses at the silkworm rite use three-horse painted peace cars.

sentences.zh: 公主有先置者，乘青交路安車，駕三。

translations.literal: Princesses who have prior placement ride green crossing-band peace chariots, hitched to three.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses already invested ride green-banded three-horse peace wagons.

sentences.zh: 諸王妃、公太夫人、夫人、縣鄉君、諸郡公侯特進夫人助蠶，乘皁交路安車，駕三。

translations.literal: The various princes’ consorts, ducal grand ladies, ladies, county and district noblewomen, and the various commandery dukes’ and marquises’ eminent ladies assisting at silkworm ride black crossing-band peace chariots, hitched to three.
translations.idiomatic: Princely consorts through county noblewomen ride black-banded three-horse peace cars at silkworm.

sentences.zh: 諸侯監國世子之世婦、侍中常侍尚書中書監令卿校世婦、命婦助蠶，乘皁交路安車，儷駕。

translations.literal: Feudal heirs’ chief wives supervising the state, palace attendant-in-ordinary and cavalry attendant-in-ordinary masters of writing secretariat director and vice ministers’ chief wives, and titled ladies assisting at silkworm ride black crossing-band peace chariots, paired hitch.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs’ wives and high inner-court ladies use black-banded peace cars with paired teams.

sentences.zh: 郡縣公侯、中二千石、二千石夫人會朝及蠶，各乘其夫之安車，皆右騑，皁交路，皁帷裳。

translations.literal: County and district dukes and marquises, and wives of full and regular two thousand piculs, for court meetings and silkworm each ride their husbands’ peace chariots, all with right trace horse, black crossing bands, black curtains and skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Noblewives attend court and silkworm in their husbands’ two-horse peace cars with black trim and right outriggers.

sentences.zh: 自非公會則不得乘軺車，止乘漆布輜軿，銅五采而已。

translations.literal: Unless for public meetings they may not ride patrol carts, only lacquered cloth enclosed wagons, bronze five colors only.
translations.idiomatic: Outside assemblies they must use lacquered cloth sedans, not patrol cars.

sentences.zh: 王妃、特進夫人、封郡君，安車，駕三，皁交路。

translations.literal: Princes’ consorts, eminent ladies, and commandery noblewomen have peace chariots, hitched to three, black crossing bands.
translations.idiomatic: High consorts and commandery ladies rate three-horse black-banded peace cars.

sentences.zh: 封縣鄉君油軿車，駕兩馬，右騑。

translations.literal: County and district noblewomen ride oil enclosed wagons, hitched to two horses, right trace horse.
translations.idiomatic: County-level titled women use oilcloth two-horse sedans with right traces.

sentences.zh: 自過江之後，舊章多缺。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, old regulations were mostly lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court fled south, most old sumptuary rules collapsed.

sentences.zh: 元帝踐極，始造大路、戎路各一，皆即古金根之制也，無復充庭之儀。

translations.literal: When Yuan Di ascended the throne, he first made a great lu and a war lu, each one, both following the ancient metal-root system, without again the court-filling display.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan commissioned one great chariot and one war car on old metal-root lines but skipped the full Han panoply.

sentences.zh: 至於郊祀大事，則權飾余車以周用。

translations.literal: As for suburban sacrifice great affairs, then they temporarily ornamented spare chariots to suffice for use.
translations.idiomatic: Major suburban rites borrowed patched-up spare wagons.

sentences.zh: 六師親征則用戎路，去其蓋而乘之，屬車但五乘而已。

translations.literal: When the six armies personally campaigned they used the war lu, removed its canopy and rode it; attendant chariots were only five in number.
translations.idiomatic: Field armies stripped the war car’s roof and cut the escort to five vehicles.

sentences.zh: 加綠油幢，硃絲路，飾青交路，黃金塗五采，其輪轂猶素，兩箱無金錦之飾。

translations.literal: They added green-oil canopy, cinnabar silk netting, ornamented green crossing bands, gold overlaid with five colors; their wheels and hubs were still plain; the two side boxes lacked gold brocade ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign gear added green canopies and red mesh but left wheels plain and sides unbroidered.

sentences.zh: 其一車又是軺車，舊儀，天子所乘駕六，是時無復六馬之乘，五路皆駕四而已，同用黑，是為玄牡。

translations.literal: One of the chariots was again a patrol cart; by old ritual the Son of Heaven rode six, but at this time there was no longer riding six horses; the five chariots all were hitched to four only, together using black—this is the dark stallion set.
translations.idiomatic: Even the patrol wagon drew four blacks; the old six-horse emperor’s team vanished—everything went four-in-hand in ink-dark bays.

sentences.zh: 無復五時車，有事則權以馬車代之，建旗其上。

translations.literal: There were no longer five-season chariots; when there was business they temporarily substituted horse carts, raising banners on them.
translations.idiomatic: Five-season colors gave way to improvised carts flying temporary standards.

sentences.zh: 其後但以五色木牛象五時車，豎旗于牛背，行則使人輿之。

translations.literal: Afterward they only used five-colored wooden oxen to imitate the five-season chariots, setting banners on the oxen’s backs; when moving they had people carry them in litters.
translations.idiomatic: Later designers painted wooden ox teams to mimic the old five-color parade.

sentences.zh: 牛之義，蓋取其負重致遠安而穩也。

translations.literal: As for the ox’s significance, it probably takes from its bearing weight and reaching far in peace and stability.
translations.idiomatic: Oxen again symbolized steady haulage.

sentences.zh: 旗常纏而不舒旆，所謂德車結旌者也。

translations.literal: The regular banners stay wound and do not unfurl pennants—this is called the virtue chariot tying its streamers.
translations.idiomatic: Pennants stayed furled—the “virtue car” look.

sentences.zh: 惟天子親戎，五旗舒旆，所謂武車綏旌者也。

translations.literal: Only when the Son of Heaven personally went to war did the five banners unfurl pennants—this is called the martial chariot relaxing its streamers.
translations.idiomatic: Only the emperor at war spread all five battle streamers.

sentences.zh: 指南車，過江亡失，及義熙五年，劉裕屠廣固，始復獲焉，乃使工人張綱補緝周用。

translations.literal: The south-pointer chariot was lost crossing the Yangzi; and in the fifth year of Yixi, Liu Yu sacked Guanggu and only then recovered it, then ordered the craftsman Zhang Gang to patch and mend it for temporary use.
translations.idiomatic: The guide car sank in the retreat until Liu Yu’s Yixi sack of Guanggu recovered one for Zhang Gang to rebuild.

sentences.zh: 十三年，裕定關中，又獲司南、記裏諸車，制度始備。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Yu pacified Guanzhong and again obtained south-pointer and mile-drum chariots; only then were the institutions complete.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years later Liu Yu’s Guanzhong campaign brought back odometer cars, completing the set.

sentences.zh: 其輦，過江亦亡制度，太元中謝安率意造焉，及破苻堅於淮上，獲京都舊輦，形制無差，大小如一，時人服其精記。

translations.literal: As for the palanquin, crossing the Yangzi also lost its institutions; in the Taiyuan period Xie An improvised one; and when he defeated Fu Jian at the Huai, he obtained the old capital palanquin, and the form and size were without difference, of one size; people of the time admired his precise memory.
translations.idiomatic: Litters were reinvented by Xie An until a captured Luoyang litter proved his memory flawless.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年，劉裕執慕容超，獲金鉦輦、豹尾，舊式猶存。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi, Liu Yu seized Murong Chao and obtained gilded-gong palanquins and leopard tails; the old style still survived.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi five’s capture of Murong Chao yielded gilded gong litters and leopard-tail regalia intact.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興三年，皇太子釋奠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Yuan’s Taixing, the heir apparent performed the school sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Taixing year three saw the crown prince’s Confucian ceremony.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「今草創，未有高車，可乘安車也。

translations.literal: The regulation said: “Now in founding beginnings, there are no high chariots; you may ride peace chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The edict admitted: “We are still improvising—use peace cars until tall state coaches exist.”

sentences.zh: 」太元中，東宮建，乘路有青赤旂，致疑。

translations.literal: ” In the Taiyuan period, when the eastern palace was built, riding lu had green and red banners, raising doubts.
translations.idiomatic: ” Later, when the heir got his own chariots, mixed green and red standards confused ritualists.

sentences.zh: 徐邈議，太子既不備五路，赤旂宜省。

translations.literal: Xu Miao argued that since the heir did not possess the five chariots, the red banner should be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao ruled the prince should drop scarlet banners without the full five-car set.

sentences.zh: 漢制，太子鸞路皆以安車為名。

translations.literal: Han institutions named all heir apparent luan lu with peace chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Han had always called the heir’s ritual car a peace-style luan.

sentences.zh: 自晉過江，禮儀疏舛，王公以下，車服卑雜，惟有東宮禮秩崇異，上次辰極，下納侯王。

translations.literal: Since Jin crossed the Yangzi, ritual was sparse and mixed; from kings and dukes downward, chariots and dress were lowly and miscellaneous; only the eastern palace ritual rank was lofty and different, ascending next to the pole star, downward admitting marquises and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Jin dress codes frayed for everyone except the heir, whose regalia alone rivaled the throne.

sentences.zh: 而安帝為皇太子乘石山安車，制如金路，義不經見，事無所出。

translations.literal: Yet when Emperor An was crown prince he rode a stone-mountain peace chariot, regulated like the metal lu; righteousness does not appear in the classics, and the matter has no source.
translations.idiomatic: An Di’s odd stone-mountain peace car aping the metal lu lacked classical warrant.

sentences.zh: 中宮初建及祀先蠶，皆用法駕，太僕妻禦，大將軍妻參乘，侍中妻陪乘，丹陽尹建康令及公卿之妻奉引，各乘其夫車服，多以宮人權領其職。

translations.literal: When the inner palace was first built and for sacrificing to the first silkworm, all used the statutory escort; the grand coachman’s wife drove, the grand general’s wife rode companion, the attendant-in-ordinary’s wife rode attendant; the Danyang governor, Jiankang magistrate, and dukes’ and ministers’ wives led the train, each riding their husbands’ chariot dress, mostly using palace women temporarily filling those posts.
translations.idiomatic: Empress silkworm rites drafted noblewomen as drivers and outriders—coachmen’s wives at the reins, generals’ wives beside them, magistrates’ wives clearing the way, often palace women standing in.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》，弁師掌六冕，司服掌六服。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the cap master controls the six crowns, and the dress master controls the six robes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou ritual split crown and robe oversight between two ministries.

sentences.zh: 自後王之制爰及庶人，各有等差。

translations.literal: From later kings’ institutions down to commoners, each had grades and differences.
translations.idiomatic: Every rank down to commoners once had fixed wardrobe rules.

sentences.zh: 及秦變古制，郊祭之服皆以袀玄，舊法掃地盡矣。

translations.literal: When Qin changed ancient institutions, suburban sacrifice dress all used plain dark silk, and old law was swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: Qin’s plain black sacrifice robes erased Zhou splendor.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦弊，西京二百餘年猶未能有所制立。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin’s abuses, and for more than two hundred years in Western Capital still could not establish institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han still had no stable court wardrobe two centuries on.

sentences.zh: 及中興後，明帝乃始采《周官》、《禮記》、《尚書》及諸儒記說，還備袞冕之服。

translations.literal: After the restoration, Emperor Ming then first took the Zhou Offices, Record of Rites, Documents, and various scholars’ records, and returned to complete the robe and crown with hanging tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han Ming Di rebuilt sacrificial dress from Zhou texts and scholars’ notes.

sentences.zh: 天子車乘冠服從歐陽氏說，公卿以下從大小夏侯氏說，始制天子、三公、九卿、特進之服，侍祠天地明堂，皆冠旒冕，兼五冕之制，一服而已。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven’s chariots, caps, and robes followed Master Ouyang’s theory; from dukes and ministers downward followed the greater and lesser Xiahou theory; he first regulated the Son of Heaven, three excellencies, nine ministers, and fully eminent nobles’ dress; when attending sacrifice to heaven and earth, bright hall, all wore tasseled crowns and held the five-crown system in one robe.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Di split sources—Ouyang for the emperor, Xiahou masters for officials—unifying heaven, earth, and hall rites under one tasseled crown system.

sentences.zh: 天子備十二章，三公諸侯用山龍九章，九卿以下用華蟲七章，皆具五采。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven fully had twelve emblems; three excellencies and feudal lords used mountain and dragon nine emblems; nine ministers downward used flower-and-insect seven emblems; all possessed five colors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore twelve symbolic motifs; dukes nine; ministers seven—each in full five-color embroidery.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝以公卿袞衣黼黻之飾，疑於至尊，多所減損，始制天子服刺繡文，公卿服織成文。

translations.literal: Wei Ming Di, because dukes’ and ministers’ sacrificial robes had axe-and-fu ornament, suspected encroachment on the supreme; he reduced much; he first regulated the Son of Heaven’s robes with embroidered patterns, dukes’ and ministers’ robes with woven patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui demoted ministerial brocade to woven patterns while reserving true embroidery for the throne.

sentences.zh: 及晉受命，遵而無改。

translations.literal: When Jin received the mandate, it followed without change.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kept Wei’s wardrobe partition.

sentences.zh: 天子郊祀天地明堂宗廟，元會臨軒，黑介幘，通天冠，平冕。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven for suburban sacrifice to heaven and earth, bright hall, and ancestral temples, and for the great New Year session facing the hall, wears black stiff cap, piercing-heaven crown, and level crown.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor wears black frame cap under the tongtian crown and flat sacrificial mian crown for heaven, hall, temple, and New Year.

sentences.zh: 冕，皁表，硃綠裏，廣七寸，長二尺二寸，加于通天冠上，前圓後方，垂白玉珠，十有二旒，以硃組為纓，無緌。

translations.literal: The crown (mian) is black outside, cinnabar and green inside, seven cun wide, two chi two cun long, placed on the piercing-heaven crown, round in front and square behind, hanging white jade beads, twelve tassels, with cinnabar cords for tassels, without dangling threads.
translations.idiomatic: The flat mian crown is black with vermilion-green lining, twelve white jade tassels, round-squared profile, cinnabar ties, no trailing fringe.

sentences.zh: 佩白玉，垂珠黃大旒，綬黃赤縹紺四采。

translations.literal: He wears white jade, hanging pearls with great yellow tassels, sash of yellow, red, light blue, and dark blue four colors.
translations.idiomatic: White jade pendants, yellow tassel strings, four-color sash.

sentences.zh: 衣皁上，絳下，前三幅，後四幅，衣畫而裳繡，為日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻之象，凡十二章。

translations.literal: The robe is black above, crimson below, three panels in front, four in back; the robe is painted and the skirt is embroidered, with images of sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, flower-and-insect, waterweed, fire, powdered grain, fu, and fu—twelve emblems in all.
translations.idiomatic: The upper robe is dyed with the twelve cosmic emblems; the lower skirt embroiders matching motifs.

sentences.zh: 素帶廣四寸，硃裏，以硃綠裨飾其側。

translations.literal: The plain belt is four cun wide, cinnabar inside, using cinnabar and green borders to ornament its sides.
translations.idiomatic: A four-inch white belt is lined red with vermilion-green edge strips.

sentences.zh: 中衣以絳緣其領袖。

translations.literal: The middle garment uses crimson to border its collar and cuffs.
translations.idiomatic: The under-robe cuffs and collar are piped in scarlet.

sentences.zh: 赤皮為韍，絳袴襪，赤舄。

translations.literal: Red leather for knee covers, crimson trousers and socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Red leather kneecaps, scarlet hose, crimson shoes.

sentences.zh: 未加元服者，空頂介幘。

translations.literal: Those who have not yet added the capping use empty-top stiff caps.
translations.idiomatic: Uncapped heirs wear open mesh frames.

sentences.zh: 其釋奠先聖，則皁紗袍，絳緣中衣，絳袴襪，黑舄，其臨軒，亦袞冕也。

translations.literal: For sacrificing to the former sage, then black gauze robe, crimson-bordered middle garment, crimson trousers and socks, black shoes; for facing the hall, also robe and crown with tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian rites use black gauze with scarlet borders; court audiences revert to full mian regalia.

sentences.zh: 其朝服，通天冠高九寸，金博山顏，黑介幘，絳紗袍，皁緣中衣。

translations.literal: For court dress, the piercing-heaven crown is nine cun high, with golden Bo Mountain on the brow, black stiff cap, cinnabar gauze robe, black-bordered middle garment.
translations.idiomatic: Daily court dress pairs a nine-inch tongtian crown with gold brow plate and scarlet gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 其拜陵，黑介幘，單衣。

translations.literal: For visiting tombs, black stiff cap, unlined garment.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb pilgrimages simplify to black cap and plain robe.

sentences.zh: 其雜服，有青赤黃白緗黑色，介幘，五色紗袍，五梁進賢冠，遠遊冠，平上幘武冠。

translations.literal: For miscellaneous dress there are green, red, yellow, white, light yellow, and black colors, stiff caps, five-color gauze robes, five-ridge worthy-advancement cap, far-roaming cap, level-top martial cap, martial cap.
translations.idiomatic: Leisure wardrobes span six hues with five-ridge scholar caps, touring caps, and martial headcloths.

sentences.zh: 其素服，白㡊單衣。

translations.literal: For plain mourning dress, white kerchief and unlined garment.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress is white headcloth over unlined coat.

sentences.zh: 後漢以來，天子之冕，前後旒用真白玉珠。

translations.literal: From Later Han onward, the Son of Heaven’s crown front and rear tassels used genuine white jade beads.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han emperors insisted on real white jade beads for the royal mian crown.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝好婦人之飾，改以珊瑚珠。

translations.literal: Wei Ming Di liked women’s ornaments and changed them to coral beads.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui famously swapped jade for coral beads.

sentences.zh: 晉初仍舊不改。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin it still followed the old without change.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin kept coral.

sentences.zh: 及過江，服章多闕，而冕飾以翡翠珊瑚雜珠。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, dress insignia were mostly lacking, yet the crown ornaments used kingfisher, coral, and mixed beads.
translations.idiomatic: Southern courts patched mian regalia with jadeite and coral mixes.

sentences.zh: 侍中顧和奏：「舊禮，冕十二旒，用白玉珠。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Gu He memorialized: “By old ritual the crown has twelve tassels using white jade beads.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He pleaded: “Classical mian crowns need twelve white jade strands.”

sentences.zh: 今美玉難得，不能備，可用白璿珠。

translations.literal: Now fine jade is hard to obtain and cannot be supplied; white spinel pearls may be used.
translations.idiomatic: ” He allowed white spinel substitutes when Hetian jade ran short.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: ” The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 通天冠，本秦制。

translations.literal: The piercing-heaven crown was originally a Qin institution.
translations.idiomatic: The tongtian crown began as Qin court gear.

sentences.zh: 高九寸，正豎，頂少斜卻，乃直下，鐵為卷梁，前有展筒，冠前加金博山述，乘輿所常服也。

translations.literal: It is nine cun high, set straight, the top slightly slanting backward, then straight down, iron forming the curled beam, with a spreading tube in front; the crown front adds golden Bo Mountain description; it is what the imperial carriage regularly wears.
translations.idiomatic: Nine inches tall with iron curl, forward “sounding tube,” and gold brow plate—it is everyday imperial headgear.

sentences.zh: 平冕，王公、卿助祭於郊廟服之。

translations.literal: The level crown: kings, dukes, and ministers wear it when assisting sacrifice at suburban altars and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and ministers wear the flat mian crown only at joint sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王公八旒，卿七旒。

translations.literal: Kings and dukes have eight tassels; ministers seven tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Princes get eight tassels, chief ministers seven.

sentences.zh: 以組為纓，色如其綬。

translations.literal: They use cords for tassels, the color like their sash.
translations.idiomatic: Tassel cords match each man’s sash colors.

sentences.zh: 王公衣山龍以下九章，卿衣華蟲以下七章。

translations.literal: Kings and dukes’ robes have mountain and dragon down to nine emblems; ministers’ robes have flower-and-insect down to seven emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Princely robes stop at nine motifs; ministers at seven.

sentences.zh: 遠遊冠，傅玄雲秦冠也。

translations.literal: The far-roaming cap: Fu Xuan says it is a Qin cap.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan traces the “far roaming” cap to Qin fashion.

sentences.zh: 似通天而前無山述，有展筒橫於冠前。

translations.literal: It resembles the piercing-heaven but lacks the mountain description in front; there is a spreading tube spanning before the crown.
translations.idiomatic: Like tongtian but without the gold brow mountain, with a horizontal tube across the brim.

sentences.zh: 皇太子及王者後、帝之兄弟、帝之子封郡王者服之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent and kings’ heirs, the emperor’s brothers, and the emperor’s sons enfeoffed as commandery kings wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Crown princes, princely heirs, imperial brothers, and sons enfeoffed as kings wear this cap.

sentences.zh: 諸王加官者自服其官之冠服，惟太子及王者後常冠焉。

translations.literal: For princes who add offices, they themselves wear that office’s cap and robes; only the heir apparent and kings’ heirs regularly wear this cap.
translations.idiomatic: Princes with extra titles wear those regalia, but heirs and princely successors keep the far-roaming cap daily.

sentences.zh: 太子則以翠羽為緌，綴以白珠，其餘但青絲而已。

translations.literal: For the heir apparent then kingfisher feathers make the tassel fringe, strung with white pearls; the rest use only blue-green silk.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince alone may trail kingfisher and pearl tassels; others use plain silk cords.

sentences.zh: 緇布冠，蔡邕雲即委貌冠也。

translations.literal: The black cloth cap: Cai Yong says it is the weimao cap.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong identifies the black cloth cap with the classical weimao.

sentences.zh: 太古冠布，齊則緇之。

translations.literal: In highest antiquity caps were cloth; for fasting then they blackened them.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient caps were undyed cloth until mourners and fasters switched to black.

sentences.zh: 緇布冠，始冠之冠也。

translations.literal: The black cloth cap is the cap of first capping.
translations.idiomatic: It is the cap placed at a young noble’s first coming-of-age rite.

sentences.zh: 其制有四形，一似武冠，又一似進賢，其一上方其下如幘顏，其一刺上而方下。

translations.literal: Its form has four shapes: one resembles the martial cap, another resembles worthy-advancement, one is square above and below like a cap’s brow, one is pointed above and square below.
translations.idiomatic: Ritualists describe four variants—some like martial caps, some like scholar caps, some squared like a headcloth profile.

sentences.zh: 行鄉射禮則公卿委貌冠，以皁絹為之。

translations.literal: When performing village archery rite, dukes and ministers wear the weimao cap, made of black silk.
translations.idiomatic: Community archery required black-silk weimao for high nobles.

sentences.zh: 形如覆杯，與皮弁同制，長七寸，高四寸。

translations.literal: The shape is like an inverted cup, same system as the skin cap, seven cun long, four cun high.
translations.idiomatic: It looks like an upside-down cup, seven by four cun, matching the leather cap mold.

sentences.zh: 衣黑而裳素，其中衣以皁緣領袖。

translations.literal: The robe is black and the skirt plain; the middle garment uses black to border collar and cuffs.
translations.idiomatic: Wear black robe, undyed skirt, black-piped under-robe.

sentences.zh: 其執事之人皮弁，以鹿皮為之。

translations.literal: Those who perform the rites wear skin caps, made of deer skin.
translations.idiomatic: Officiants switch to soft deer-skin bian caps.

sentences.zh: 進賢冠，古緇布遺象也，斯蓋文儒者之服。

translations.literal: The worthy-advancement cap is the surviving image of ancient black cloth; this is generally scholar dress.
translations.idiomatic: The ridged “worthy” cap descends from the black cloth prototype—standard literati headgear.

sentences.zh: 前高七寸，後高三寸，長八寸，有五梁、三梁、二梁、一梁。

translations.literal: The front is seven cun high, the rear three cun high, eight cun long, having five ridges, three ridges, two ridges, or one ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Its profile slopes from seven cun in front to three behind, with one to five horizontal ridges denoting rank.

sentences.zh: 人主元服，始加緇布，則冠五梁進賢。

translations.literal: When the ruler first caps with the first rites, he first adds black cloth, then caps five-ridge worthy-advancement.
translations.idiomatic: An emperor’s first capping pairs black cloth with the five-ridge scholar cap.

sentences.zh: 三公及封郡公、縣公、郡侯、縣侯、鄉亭侯，則冠三梁。

translations.literal: The three excellencies and enfeoffed commandery dukes, county dukes, commandery marquises, county marquises, and village and pavilion marquises then cap three ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises of every tier wear three ridges.

sentences.zh: 卿、大夫、八座，尚書，關中內侯、二千石及千石以上，則冠兩梁。

translations.literal: Ministers, grandees, the eight seats, masters of writing, interior marquises at the passes, two thousand piculs and one thousand piculs and above, then cap two ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers and two-thousand-bushel ranks take two ridges.

sentences.zh: 中書郎、秘書丞郎、著作郎、尚書丞郎、太子洗馬舍人、六百石以下至於令史、門郎、小史、並冠一梁。

translations.literal: Secretariat gentlemen, palace library assistants and gentlemen, editorial gentlemen, masters of writing assistants and gentlemen, heir apparent scribes and housemen, six hundred piculs down to record clerks, gate gentlemen, and petty clerks all cap one ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Mid- and low-level secretaries and clerks wear the single-ridge cap.

sentences.zh: 漢建初中，太官令冠兩梁，親省禦膳為重也。

translations.literal: In Han’s Jianchu mid-period, the grand provisioner director capped two ridges, because personally inspecting imperial meals was weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Even the imperial chef once rated two ridges when tasting the sovereign’s food.

sentences.zh: 博士兩梁，崇儒也。

translations.literal: Doctors of erudition two ridges, honoring Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians alone merited two ridges to mark learning.

sentences.zh: 宗室劉氏亦得兩梁冠，示加服也。

translations.literal: Imperial clan Liu surnames also obtained two-ridge caps, showing added dress.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kinsmen Liu could earn two ridges as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 武冠，一名武弁，一名大冠，一名繁冠，一名建冠，一名籠冠，即古之惠文冠。

translations.literal: The martial cap, one name martial bian, one name great cap, one name many-layer cap, one name founded cap, one name cage cap, is the ancient Huizwen cap.
translations.idiomatic: The tall “martial” cap—also called the great cap or cage cap—is the old Huizwen style.

sentences.zh: 或曰趙惠文王所造，因以為名。

translations.literal: Some say King Huiwen of Zhao created it, therefore took the name.
translations.idiomatic: Legend credits King Huiwen of Zhao with inventing it.

sentences.zh: 亦云，惠者蟪也，其冠文輕細如蟬翼，故名惠文。

translations.literal: It is also said “hui” means cicada; the cap’s pattern is light and fine like cicada wings, therefore named Huizwen.
translations.idiomatic: Others derive “hui” from “cicada,” noting the gauze weave mimics wings.

sentences.zh: 或云，齊人見千歲涸澤之神，名曰慶忌，冠大冠，乘小車，好疾馳，因象其冠而服焉。

translations.literal: Some say Qi people saw a thousand-year spirit of a dried marsh named Qingji, wearing a great cap, riding a small cart, fond of swift gallop, therefore imitated his cap and wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Another tale ties it to the marsh spirit Qingji, who raced in a tall cap.

sentences.zh: 漢幸臣閎孺為侍中，皆服大冠。

translations.literal: Han favorite Hong Ru as attendant-in-ordinary all wore the great cap.
translations.idiomatic: Han favorites like Hong Ru sported the great cap at court.

sentences.zh: 天子元服亦先加大冠，左右侍臣及諸將軍武官通服之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven first caps he also first adds the great cap; left and right attendant ministers and various generals and martial officials generally wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors began capping with the great cap, as did generals and close attendants.

sentences.zh: 侍中、常侍則加金璫，附蟬為飾，插以貂毛，黃金為竿，侍中插左，常侍插右。

translations.literal: For attendant-in-ordinary and regular attendant then add golden dang, attaching cicada as ornament, inserting sable fur, yellow gold as shaft; attendant-in-ordinary inserts left, regular attendant inserts right.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants add gold disks, jade cicadas, and sable plumes—left for attendants-in-ordinary, right for regular attendants.

sentences.zh: 胡廣曰：「昔趙武靈王為胡服，以金貂飾首。

translations.literal: Hu Guang said: “Formerly King Wuling of Zhao made Hu dress, ornamenting the head with gold sable.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang recalled how Zhao Wuling’s “Hu robes” paired with gilded sable hats.

sentences.zh: 秦滅趙，以其君冠賜侍臣。

translations.literal: Qin destroyed Zhao and conferred its ruler’s cap on attendant ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Qin seized Zhao’s royal cap style for palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 」應劭《漢官》云：「說者以為金取剛強，百煉不耗。

translations.literal: ” Ying Shuo’s Han Offices says: “Expositors take gold as hard, refined by fire without loss.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ying Shuo adds that gold symbolizes incorruptibility.

sentences.zh: 蟬居高飲清，口在掖下。

translations.literal: The cicada dwells high and drinks purity, its mouth under the armpit.
translations.idiomatic: Cicadas “drink dew” aloft—an emblem of purity.

sentences.zh: 貂內勁悍而外柔縟。

translations.literal: The sable is fierce within yet soft without.
translations.idiomatic: Sable stands for inner strength beneath a supple pelt.

sentences.zh: 」又以蟬取清高飲露而不食，貂則紫蔚柔潤而毛采不彰灼，金則貴其寶瑩，於義亦有所取。

translations.literal: ” Moreover because the cicada takes being pure and high, drinking dew and not eating, while the sable is purple luxuriant soft moist and its fur sheen is not glaring, and gold esteems its precious gleam—in meaning each has something taken.
translations.idiomatic: ” Later writers piled meanings: cicadas for abstinent purity, sable for modest brilliance, gold for precious integrity.

sentences.zh: 或以為北土多寒，胡人常以貂皮溫額，後世效此，遂以附冠。

translations.literal: Some think the northern land is very cold; Hu people constantly used sable fur to warm the forehead; later generations imitated this, then attached it to the cap.
translations.idiomatic: Pragmatists note northern riders wrapped sable across the brow for warmth, which became court fashion.

sentences.zh: 漢貂用赤黑色，王莽用黃貂，各附服色所尚也。

translations.literal: Han sable used red-black; Wang Mang used yellow sable, each attaching to the dress color honored.
translations.idiomatic: Han favored dark sable; Wang Mang switched to yellow to match his color theory.

sentences.zh: 高山冠，一名側注，高九寸，鐵為卷梁，制似通天。

translations.literal: The high-mountain cap, one name side pour, nine cun high, iron forming the curled beam, system like piercing-heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The “high mountain” or side-tilt cap rises nine cun with an iron roll like tongtian.

sentences.zh: 頂直豎，不斜卻，無山述展筒。

translations.literal: The top stands straight, not slanting backward, without mountain description spreading tube.
translations.idiomatic: Unlike tongtian it stands plumb without brow plate or sounding tube.

sentences.zh: 高山者，《詩》云「高山仰止」，取其矜莊賓遠者也。

translations.literal: “High mountain” means, the Odes says “high mountain, look up and stop,” taking its dignity and keeping guests far.
translations.idiomatic: The name quotes the Odes—evoking lofty dignity that keeps onlookers at reverent distance.

sentences.zh: 中外官、謁者、謁者僕射所服。

translations.literal: Central and outer officials, ushers, and usher directors wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Heralds and court ushers wear this cap.

sentences.zh: 胡廣曰：「高山，齊王冠也。

translations.literal: Hu Guang said: “High mountain is the Qi king’s cap.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang calls it the old Qi royal cap.

sentences.zh: 傅曰'桓公好高冠大帶'。

translations.literal: The tradition says 'Lord Huan loved tall caps and broad belts.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi supposedly loved outsized caps and sashes.

sentences.zh: 秦滅齊，以其君冠賜謁者近臣。

translations.literal: Qin destroyed Qi and conferred its ruler’s cap on ushers and close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Qin gave Qi’s kingly cap to palace heralds.

sentences.zh: 」應劭曰：「高山，今法冠也，秦行人使官亦服之。

translations.literal: ” Ying Shuo said: “High mountain is today’s law cap; Qin envoys and traveling officials also wore it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ying Shuo equates it with the later “law cap” of Qin envoys.

sentences.zh: 」而《漢官儀》云「乘輿冠高山之冠，飛翮之纓」，然則天子亦有時服焉。

translations.literal: ” And Han Offices Protocol says “the imperial carriage caps the high-mountain cap, flying-feather tassels,” thus the Son of Heaven also sometimes wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Han protocol even shows emperors occasionally donning it with feather tassels.

sentences.zh: 《傅子》曰：「魏明帝以其制似通天、遠遊，故改令卑下。」

translations.literal: The Master Fu says: “Wei Ming Di because its system resembled piercing-heaven and far-roaming, therefore ordered it made lower.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan notes Cao Rui lowered the cap because it rivaled imperial silhouettes.

sentences.zh: 法冠，一名柱後，或謂之獬豸冠。

translations.literal: The law cap, one name pillar rear, some call it the xiezhi cap.
translations.idiomatic: The “law cap,” or pillar-back hat, is the unicorn-judge style.

sentences.zh: 高五寸，以縰為展筒。

translations.literal: Five cun high, using fine cloth for spreading tube.
translations.idiomatic: It stands five cun with a gauze “sounding” tube.

sentences.zh: 鐵為柱卷，取其不曲撓也。

translations.literal: Iron makes the pillar curl, taking its not bending.
translations.idiomatic: Iron stiffeners symbolize unbending justice.

sentences.zh: 侍御史、廷尉正監平，凡執法官皆服之。

translations.literal: Attending censors, commandant of justice rectifiers and overseers, in general all law officials wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and court inspectors wear it as their badge.

sentences.zh: 或謂獬豸神羊，能觸邪佞。

translations.literal: Some say the xiezhi is a divine ram able to strike the crooked and flattering.
translations.idiomatic: Myth calls the xiezhi a one-horn ram that gores the unjust.

sentences.zh: 《異物志》云：「北荒之中，有獸名獬豸，一角，性別曲直。

translations.literal: The Record of Strange Creatures says: “In the northern wilds there is a beast named xiezhi, one horn, nature distinguishing crooked and straight.
translations.idiomatic: A bestiary places the xiezhi in the northern wastes with a single horn to judge right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 見人鬥，觸不直者。

translations.literal: Seeing people fight, it gores the not straight.
translations.idiomatic: In brawls it butts the guilty party.

sentences.zh: 聞人爭，咋不正者。

translations.literal: Hearing people quarrel, it bites the not correct.
translations.idiomatic: In quarrels it snaps at the liar.

sentences.zh: 楚王嘗獲此獸，因象其形以制衣冠。

translations.literal: The king of Chu once captured this beast, then modeled its form to make cap and robe.
translations.idiomatic: A king of Chu supposedly modeled court dress on the creature.

sentences.zh: 」胡廣曰：「《春秋左氏傳》晉侯觀於軍府，見鐘儀，曰'南冠而縶者誰也'？

translations.literal: ” Hu Guang said: “In Zuo’s Spring and Autumn Commentary the marquis of Jin inspected the army storehouse, saw Zhong Yi, and said ‘The southern cap and bound one—who is he?’
translations.idiomatic: ” Hu Guang links it to the “southern cap” prisoner in Zuo’s Commentary.

sentences.zh: 南冠即楚冠。

translations.literal: The southern cap is the Chu cap.
translations.idiomatic: That “southern cap” meant Chu headgear.

sentences.zh: 秦滅楚，以其冠服賜執法臣也。」

translations.literal: Qin destroyed Chu and conferred its cap and robe on law-executing ministers.”
translations.idiomatic: Qin repurposed Chu’s judge hat for censors.

sentences.zh: 長冠，一名齊冠。

translations.literal: The long cap, one name Qi cap.
translations.idiomatic: The “long cap” is also called the Qi-style crown.

sentences.zh: 高七寸，廣三寸，漆纚為之，制如版，以竹為裏。

translations.literal: Seven cun high, three cun wide, lacquered gauze makes it; the system is like a board, bamboo as inner frame.
translations.idiomatic: Seven by three cun, board-shaped, built on a bamboo frame with lacquered mesh.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖微時，以竹皮為此冠，其世因謂劉氏冠。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu was lowly, he used bamboo skin for this cap; his age therefore called it the Liu clan cap.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bang invented a bamboo-skin version later nicknamed the Liu family cap.

sentences.zh: 後除竹用漆纚。

translations.literal: Afterward they removed bamboo and used lacquered gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Later makers replaced bamboo with lacquer-soaked silk.

sentences.zh: 司馬彪曰：「長冠蓋楚制。

translations.literal: Sima Biao said: “The long cap is probably Chu system.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao traces it to southern Chu fashion.

sentences.zh: 人間或謂之鵲尾冠，非也。

translations.literal: People sometimes call it the magpie-tail cap; that is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Folk wrongly call it a “magpie tail.”

sentences.zh: 救日蝕則服長冠，而祠宗廟諸祀冠之。

translations.literal: When rescuing solar eclipse they wear the long cap, and for sacrificing to the ancestral temple various sacrifices they cap it.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers wore it for eclipse rites; it became temple dress.

sentences.zh: 此高祖所造，後世以為祭服，尊敬之至也。」

translations.literal: This is what Gaozu created; later generations took it as sacrificial dress, utmost veneration.”
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Bang’s creation it became sacrificial headwear of highest respect.

sentences.zh: 建華冠，以鐵為柱卷，貫大銅珠九枚，古用雜木珠，原憲所冠華冠是也。

translations.literal: The splendor-blossom cap uses iron for pillar curl, piercing nine great copper beads; antiquity used mixed wood beads; what Yuan Xian capped as splendor cap is this.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual “splendor” cap threads nine bronze beads on iron—Yuan Xian’s tall cap was this type.

sentences.zh: 又《春秋左氏傳》鄭子臧好聚鷸冠，謂建華是也。

translations.literal: Moreover Zuo’s Spring and Autumn Commentary: Zang of Zheng loved gathering kingfisher caps, called splendor-blossom is this.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo tells of Zheng prince Zang’s kingfisher “splendor” cap—same family.

sentences.zh: 祀天地、五郊、明堂，舞人服之。

translations.literal: For sacrificing to heaven and earth, five suburbs, and bright hall, dancers wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Altar dancers still wear it for heaven, earth, five directions, and hall rites.

sentences.zh: 漢《育命舞》樂人所服。

translations.literal: Han Nurture Destiny dancers wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Han “Nurture Destiny” musicians used it.

sentences.zh: 方山冠，其制似進賢。

translations.literal: The square-mountain cap, its system resembles worthy-advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The square-mountain cap copies the scholar-cap profile.

sentences.zh: 鄭展曰：「方山冠，以五采縠為之。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhan said: “The square-mountain cap uses five-color gauze to make it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhan describes multicolored gauze panels.

sentences.zh: 」漢《大予》、《八佾》、《五行》樂人所服，冠衣各如其行方之色而舞焉。

translations.literal: ” Han Grand Music, eight rows, and Five Agents musicians wore it; cap and robe each matched their row’s color direction and danced.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Music performers matched cap colors to the five directions.

sentences.zh: 巧士冠，前高七寸，要後相通，直豎。

translations.literal: The clever-gentleman cap, seven cun high in front, the waist and rear connecting, standing straight.
translations.idiomatic: The “clever gentleman” cap is a tall straight front-to-back piece.

sentences.zh: 此冠不常用，漢氏惟郊天，黃門從官四人冠之；

translations.literal: This cap is not commonly used; Han only at suburban heaven, four yellow-gate followers capped it;
translations.idiomatic: Han emperors used it rarely—four yellow-gate runners at suburban heaven rites.

sentences.zh: 在鹵簿中，夾乘輿車前，以備宦者四星。

translations.literal: Within the escort, flanking the imperial carriage front, to supply the four eunuch stars.
translations.idiomatic: They flanked the chariot to symbolize the four “eunuch” constellations.

sentences.zh: 或云，掃除從官所服。

translations.literal: Some say it is what sweepers and followers wear.
translations.idiomatic: Others say it marked sweepers in train.

sentences.zh: 卻非冠，高五寸，制似長冠。

translations.literal: The “reject wrong” cap, five cun high, system like long cap.
translations.idiomatic: The five-inch “reject wrong” cap resembles the long cap.

sentences.zh: 宮殿門吏僕射冠之。

translations.literal: Palace gate clerks and gate directors cap it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gatekeepers wear it.

sentences.zh: 負赤幡，青翅燕尾，諸僕射幡皆如之。

translations.literal: They bear red banners, green wings swallow-tail; the various directors’ banners are all like this.
translations.idiomatic: They carry red swallow-tailed banners like other gate officers.

sentences.zh: 卻敵冠，前高四寸，通長四寸，後高三寸，制似進賢。

translations.literal: The “repel enemy” cap, four cun high in front, four cun total length, three cun high in rear, system like worthy-advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The “repel foe” cap is a compact scholar-cap profile for guards.

sentences.zh: 凡當殿門衛士服之。

translations.literal: In general hall gate guards wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Hall sentinels at palace doors use it.

sentences.zh: 樊噲冠，廣九寸，高七寸，前後出各四寸，制似平冕。

translations.literal: The Fan Kuai cap, nine cun wide, seven cun high, front and rear each protruding four cun, system like level crown.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai’s cap is nine by seven cun with four-cun brims, shaped like the flat sacrificial crown.

sentences.zh: 昔楚漢會於鴻門，項籍圖危高祖，樊噲常持鐵楯，聞急，乃裂裳苞楯，戴以為冠，排入羽營，因數羽罪，漢王乘間得出。

translations.literal: Formerly Chu and Han met at Hongmen; Xiang Yu plotted danger to the High Ancestor; Fan Kuai always held an iron shield; hearing urgency, then tore skirt wrapping the shield, wore it as cap, pushed into the feather camp, then enumerated Yu’s crimes; the king of Han took the gap and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongmen Fan Kuai ripped his skirt, wrapped his shield as a makeshift cap, burst into Xiang Yu’s camp, and berated him until Liu Bang slipped away.

sentences.zh: 後人壯其意，乃制冠象焉。

translations.literal: Later people admired his intent, then made a cap imitating it.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations immortalized the gesture in a formal cap.

sentences.zh: 凡殿門司馬衛士服之。

translations.literal: In general hall gate marshals and guards wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gate marshals wear the Fan Kuai style.

sentences.zh: 術氏冠，前圓，吳制，差池四重。

translations.literal: The Shu clan cap, round in front, Wu system, staggered four layers.
translations.idiomatic: The round-front Wu-style “Shu” cap stacks four tiers.

sentences.zh: 趙武靈王好服之。

translations.literal: King Wuling of Zhao liked to wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wuling favored it.

sentences.zh: 或曰，楚莊王復仇冠是也。

translations.literal: Some say it is the Chu Zhuang king revenge cap.
translations.idiomatic: Others link it to King Zhuang of Chu’s “vengeance” crown.

sentences.zh: 鶡冠，加雙鶡尾，豎插兩邊。

translations.literal: The he cap adds double he tail feathers, vertically inserted on two sides.
translations.idiomatic: The he warrior cap mounts twin pheasant tails upright.

sentences.zh: 鶡，鳥名也，形類鷂而微黑，性果勇，其鬥到死乃止。

translations.literal: He is a bird name; its form resembles a goshawk but slightly black; its nature is indeed brave; its fights until death then stop.
translations.idiomatic: The he is a fierce blackish hawk that fights to the death.

sentences.zh: 上党貢之，趙武靈王以表顯壯士。

translations.literal: Shangdang presented them; King Wuling of Zhao used them to display brave men.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdang sent the feathers; Zhao Wuling awarded them to champions.

sentences.zh: 至秦漢，猶施之武人。

translations.literal: Down to Qin and Han, they still applied them to martial men.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han warriors still wore he plumes.

sentences.zh: 皮弁，以鹿皮淺毛黃白色者為之。

translations.literal: The skin bian uses deer skin with shallow fur yellow-white to make it.
translations.idiomatic: The bian cap uses pale yellow deerskin.

sentences.zh: 《禮》「王皮弁，會五采玉，象邸玉笄」，謂之合皮為弁。

translations.literal: The Rites: “The king’s skin bian joins five-color jade, elephant foot-stool jade hairpin,” called joining skins to make bian.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites describe the king’s bian seamed with five-color jade and ivory hairpins.

sentences.zh: 其縫中名曰會，以采玉硃為。

translations.literal: Its seam middle is called hui, using colored jade and vermilion to make.
translations.idiomatic: The crown seam junction is called the hui, inlaid with colored jade.

sentences.zh: ，結也。

translations.literal: , meaning “to knot.”
translations.idiomatic: The following gloss reads “fastened,” explaining the hairpin’s knot.

sentences.zh: 天子五采，諸侯三采。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven five colors; feudal lords three colors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors use five jade hues; lords three.

sentences.zh: 邸，冠下抵也，象骨為之，音帝也。

translations.literal: Di means the cap’s lower rest; elephant bone makes it, pronounced like di.
translations.idiomatic: The “di” block under the cap is carved ivory, homophone to “emperor.”

sentences.zh: 天子則縫十二，公侯伯七，子男五，孤四，卿大夫三。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven then has twelve seams; dukes, marquises, and earls seven; viscounts and barons five; solitary four; ministers and grandees three.
translations.idiomatic: Seam counts mark rank—twelve for the throne down to three for ministers.

sentences.zh: 韋弁，制似皮弁，頂上尖，韎草染之，色如淺絳。

translations.literal: The leather bian, system like skin bian, pointed on top, dyed with wei grass, color like light crimson.
translations.idiomatic: The leather bian resembles the deer cap but peaks sharper, dyed pink-crimson with wei herb.

sentences.zh: 爵弁，一名廣冕。

translations.literal: The duke bian, one name wide mian.
translations.idiomatic: The “duke” bian is also called the broad sacrificial crown.

sentences.zh: 高八寸，長尺二寸，如爵形，前小後大。

translations.literal: Eight cun high, one chi two cun long, like a duke-vessel shape, small in front, large in rear.
translations.idiomatic: It stands eight cun, spans a foot two, shaped like a ritual jue cup—narrow in front, broad behind.

sentences.zh: 增其上似爵頭色。

translations.literal: They enlarge the upper part like a jue head color.
translations.idiomatic: The crown mimics the flared lip of a bronze jue.

sentences.zh: 有收持笄，所謂夏收殷哻者也。

translations.literal: It has gathered hairpin holders; this is what is called Xia shou and Yin han (text reads 哻).
translations.idiomatic: It keeps the ancient hairpin loops associated with Xia and Shang court caps.

sentences.zh: 祠天地、五郊、明堂，《雲翹舞》樂人服之。

translations.literal: For sacrificing to heaven and earth, five suburbs, and bright hall, Cloud Wing dancers wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Altar dancers in the “Cloud Wing” suite wear this crown.

sentences.zh: 幘者，古賤人不冠者之服也。

translations.literal: The headcloth is what ancient lowly people who did not cap wore.
translations.idiomatic: The ze was originally headwrap for commoners barred from formal caps.

sentences.zh: 漢元帝額有壯發，始引幘服之。

translations.literal: Han Yuandi had a strong hairline on the forehead, then first drew the headcloth and wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Han hid a prominent hairline with a ze wrap, starting a fad.

sentences.zh: 王莽頂禿，又加其屋也。

translations.literal: Wang Mang was bald on top, again added its roof.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang stacked a higher roof to cover his bald crown.

sentences.zh: 《漢注》曰，冠進賢者宜長耳，今介幘也。

translations.literal: Han Commentary says, those who cap worthy-advancement should have long ears; today’s stiff cap.
translations.idiomatic: Han notes pair long “ears” with scholar caps—ancestors of the stiff court ze.

sentences.zh: 冠惠文者宜短耳，今平上幘也。

translations.literal: Those who cap Huizwen should have short ears; today’s level-top ze.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Huizwen caps use short ears—the level-top ze line.

sentences.zh: 始時各隨所宜，遂因冠為別。

translations.literal: At first each followed what was fitting, then followed the cap to make distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Styles diverged until cap type dictated ze shape.

sentences.zh: 介幘服文吏，平上幘服武官也。

translations.literal: Stiff caps dress civil clerks; level-top ze dress martial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Civil versus military headwraps became fixed.

sentences.zh: 童子幘無屋者，示不成人也。

translations.literal: Children’s ze without roof shows not yet adult.
translations.idiomatic: Boys wear roofless zes until capping.

sentences.zh: 又有納言幘，幘後收又一重，方三寸。

translations.literal: Moreover there is the “inner edict” ze, the ze rear gathered again one layer, square three cun.
translations.idiomatic: Palace “inner edict” zes add a triple-cun rear fold.

sentences.zh: 又有赤幘，騎吏、武吏、乘輿鼓吹所服。

translations.literal: Moreover there is the red ze, worn by mounted clerks, martial clerks, and imperial musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Red zes mark outriders, guards, and imperial bands.

sentences.zh: 救日蝕，文武官皆免冠著幘，對朝服，示武威也。

translations.literal: When rescuing solar eclipse, civil and martial officials all remove caps and wear zes, facing court dress, showing martial awe.
translations.idiomatic: During eclipse rites everyone doffed caps for red zes over court robes as a martial gesture.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，立秋日獵，服緗幘。

translations.literal: Han ritual: on Liqiu hunt day they wore light-yellow zes.
translations.idiomatic: Han autumn hunts required buff-colored zes.

sentences.zh: 及江左，哀帝從博士曹弘之等議，立秋禦讀令，改用素白㡊。

translations.literal: When it came to Jiangzuo, Emperor Ai followed doctors Cao Hongzhi and others’ proposal: for the Liqiu imperial edict ceremony they changed to plain white kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin Ai Di switched Liqiu court dress to plain white scarves per scholars’ advice.

sentences.zh: 案漢末王公名士多委王服，以幅巾為雅，是以袁紹、崔鈞之徒，雖為將帥，皆著縑巾。

translations.literal: According to investigation, late Han kings, dukes, and famous gentlemen mostly cast off kingly dress, taking plain headcloth as elegant; therefore Yuan Shao, Cui Jun and the like, although generals, all wore thin-silk headcloths.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han elites favored simple headcloths—even generals like Yuan Shao wore plain silk wraps.

sentences.zh: 魏武以天下凶荒，資財乏匱，擬古皮弁，裁縑帛以為㡊，合乎簡易隨時之義，以色別其貴賤，本施軍飾，非為國容也。

translations.literal: Wei Wu because the realm was violent and famine, goods and wealth exhausted, modeled ancient skin bian, cutting silk to make kerchief, matching simple ease suiting the times’ meaning, using color to distinguish noble and base; originally applied as military dress, not as state appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao issued colored silk “kerchief-caps” during famine to simplify military dress, not formal regalia.

sentences.zh: 徐爰曰：「俗說㡊本未有岐，荀文若巾之行，觸樹枝成岐，謂之為善，因而弗改。

translations.literal: Xu Ai said: “Popular story says the kerchief originally had no fork; when Xun Wenruo’s kerchief walked, it touched a tree branch forming a fork; they called it auspicious, therefore did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai tells how Xun Yu’s kerchief snagged into lucky forked tails that became fashion.

sentences.zh: 」今通以為慶吊服。

translations.literal: ” Now it is generally taken as congratulation and mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: ” Later society adopted forked kerchiefs for both joyous and funerary wear.

sentences.zh: 巾，以葛為之，形如㡊而橫著之，古尊卑共服也。

translations.literal: The headcloth uses kudzu to make it; the shape is like a kerchief but worn horizontally; ancient noble and base together wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Ge-cloth scarves, worn sideways like caps, were once universal.

sentences.zh: 故漢末妖賊以黃為巾，世謂黃巾賊。

translations.literal: Therefore late Han rebel bandits used yellow as headcloth; the age called them Yellow Turban bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Yellow Turbans took their name from saffron scarves.

sentences.zh: 帽名猶冠也，義取于蒙覆其首，其本纚也。

translations.literal: The hat’s name is still “crown”; the meaning takes from covering the head; its origin is the fine mesh wrap.
translations.idiomatic: “Hat” functionally replaced “crown,” evolving from hair mesh.

sentences.zh: 古者冠無幘，冠下有纚，以繒為之。

translations.literal: In antiquity crowns had no ze; below the crown there was li, made of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Early crowns used silk hairnets instead of zes.

sentences.zh: 後世施幘於冠，因或裁纓為帽。

translations.literal: Later generations applied ze to crowns, then sometimes cut tassels into hats.
translations.idiomatic: Later courts fused ze with crown and tailored brimmed hats.

sentences.zh: 自乘輿宴居，下至庶人無爵者皆服之。

translations.literal: From the imperial carriage at leisure down to commoners without rank all wear them.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone from the emperor at leisure to commoners wears soft hats.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸和九年，制聽尚書八座丞郎、門下三省侍官乘車，白㡊低幃，出入掖門。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng’s ninth Xianhe year, regulation allowed masters of writing eight seats assistants and gentlemen, gate and three departments attendant officials, to ride carts, white kerchief low curtain, entering and leaving the side palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe nine let senior clerks ride through side gates in white scarves and low screens.

sentences.zh: 又，二宮直官著烏紗㡊。

translations.literal: Moreover, two-palace duty officials wear black gauze kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Palace watch officers don black gauze caps.

sentences.zh: 然則往往士人宴居皆著㡊矣。

translations.literal: Thus commonly gentlemen at leisure all wore kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon every scholar lounged in kerchief caps.

sentences.zh: 而江左時野人已著帽，人士亦往往而然，但其頂圓耳，後乃高其屋雲。

translations.literal: Yet in Jiangzuo times rustics already wore hats; gentlemen also often did so, but their tops were round; afterward they raised the roof, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners borrowed peasants’ round hats, then heightened the crown for fashion.

sentences.zh: 漢制，自天子至於百官，無不佩劍，其後惟朝帶劍。

translations.literal: Han institutions: from the Son of Heaven down to the hundred officials, none did not wear swords; afterward only at court did they belt swords.
translations.idiomatic: Han once required swords for all ranks; later only court audiences kept the habit.

sentences.zh: 晉世始代之以木，貴者猶用玉首，賤者亦用蚌、金銀、玳瑁為雕飾。

translations.literal: The Jin age first replaced them with wood; the noble still used jade heads; the base also used mussel, gold, silver, and tortoiseshell for carved ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Jin switched to wooden blades with jade or shell hilts by rank.

sentences.zh: 乘輿六璽，秦制也。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage six seals is Qin system.
translations.idiomatic: Six imperial jades follow Qin precedent.

sentences.zh: 曰「皇帝行璽」、「皇帝之璽」、「皇帝信璽」、「天子行璽」、「天子之璽」、「天子信璽」，漢遵秦不改。

translations.literal: They are called “Emperor traveling seal,” “Emperor’s seal,” “Emperor trust seal,” “Heavenly Son traveling seal,” “Heavenly Son’s seal,” “Heavenly Son trust seal”; Han followed Qin without change.
translations.idiomatic: The six mottoes—three for “emperor,” three for “Son of Heaven”—survived unchanged from Qin into Han.

sentences.zh: 又有秦始皇藍田玉璽，螭獸紐，在六璽之外，文曰「受天之命，皇帝壽昌」。

translations.literal: Moreover there is the First Emperor of Qin’s Lantian jade seal, chi-beast knob, outside the six seals; the inscription reads “Receiving heaven’s mandate, the emperor long prosperous.”
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the six sits the Lantian jade heirloom with horned-dragon knob and cosmic motto.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖佩之，後世名曰傳國璽，與斬白蛇劍俱為乘輿所寶。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu wore it; later generations named it the transmission-of-state seal, together with the white-snake-slaying sword treasured by the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bang claimed both the “transmission seal” and the snake sword as regalia.

sentences.zh: 斬白蛇劍至惠帝時武庫火燒之，遂亡。

translations.literal: The white-snake-slaying sword reached Emperor Hui when the armory fire burned it, then was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The fabled sword burned in Wei’s Luoyang armory conflagration.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝沒胡，傳國璽沒于劉聰，後又沒于石勒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai fell to the Hu, the transmission seal was lost to Liu Cong, afterward again lost to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: The seal passed from Jin captivity to Liu Cong, then Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 及石季龍死，胡亂，穆帝世乃還江南。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong died, Hu chaos; in Emperor Mu’s age it then returned south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: It resurfaced in the south only after Shi Hu’s death and turmoil.

sentences.zh: 革帶，古之鞶帶也，謂之鞶革，文武眾官牧守丞令下及騶寺皆服之。

translations.literal: The leather belt is the ancient pan belt, called pan leather; civil and martial multitude of officials, shepherds, guards, magistrates down to outriders and temple attendants all wear it.
translations.idiomatic: The leather “pan” belt girds everyone from magistrates to outriders.

sentences.zh: 其有囊綬，則以綴於革帶，其戎服則以皮絡帶代之。

translations.literal: If there is sash pouch, then attach it to the leather belt; for martial dress then substitute leather net belts.
translations.idiomatic: Civil belts carry purple sash bags; field dress swaps in leather mesh.

sentences.zh: 八坐尚書荷紫，以生紫為袷囊，綴之服外，加于左肩。

translations.literal: The eight seats masters of writing bear purple, using raw purple for lapel pouch, attaching it outside the robe on the left shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers wear purple document pouches slung from the left shoulder.

sentences.zh: 昔周公負成王，制此服衣，至今以為朝服。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou carried King Cheng on his back, making this robe; down to today it is taken as court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Myth credits the Zhou regent’s baby-carrying sash for today’s court pouch.

sentences.zh: 或云漢世用盛奏事，負之以行，未詳也。

translations.literal: Some say Han generations used it to hold memorials, carrying them on the back; not detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Others say Han clerks slung memorial tubes there—uncertain.

sentences.zh: 車前五百者，卿行旅從，五百人為一旅。

translations.literal: The five hundred before the chariot: ministers’ processions follow, five hundred men make one brigade.
translations.idiomatic: “Five hundred front” recalled a full brigade escorting ministers.

sentences.zh: 漢氏一統，故去其人，留其名也。

translations.literal: The Han house unified the realm, therefore removed the men but kept the name.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept the title after disbanding the real five-hundred guard.

sentences.zh: 袴褶之制，未詳所起，近世凡車駕親戎、中外戒嚴服之。

translations.literal: The trousers-and-jacket system’s origin is not detailed; in recent generations whenever the chariot personally campaigns inside and outside alert they wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Military tunics and riding breeches appear for imperial campaigns and palace alerts.

sentences.zh: 服無定色，冠黑帽，綴紫摽，摽以繒為之，長四寸，廣一寸，腰有絡帶以代鞶。

translations.literal: Dress has no fixed color; cap black hat, attaching purple streamer tag; the tag is made of silk, four cun long, one cun wide; the waist has net belt replacing pan.
translations.idiomatic: Alert dress uses black hats with purple silk markers and mesh waistbands.

sentences.zh: 中官紫摽，外官絳摽。

translations.literal: Inner officials purple tags; outer officials crimson tags.
translations.idiomatic: Palace staff wear purple tabs; field officers crimson.

sentences.zh: 又有纂嚴戎服而不綴摽，行留文武悉同。

translations.literal: Moreover there is assembled strict martial dress without attaching tags; stationary and traveling civil and martial are all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Full mobilization dress drops the streamer tags but otherwise matches.

sentences.zh: 其畋獵巡幸，則惟從官戎服帶鞶革，文官不下纓，武官脫冠。

translations.literal: For hunting and touring, then only followers wear martial dress with pan leather belts; civil officials do not lower tassels; martial officials remove caps.
translations.idiomatic: On hunts, civil aides keep tassels up while soldiers shed formal caps.

sentences.zh: 漢制，一歲五郊，天子與執事者所服各如方色，百官不執事者服常服絳衣以從。

translations.literal: Han institutions: one year five suburbs; the Son of Heaven and those who officiate wear colors matching each direction; the hundred officials who do not officiate wear regular dress crimson robes to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Han suburban rounds color-coded officiants while others wore plain crimson.

sentences.zh: 魏秘書監秦靜曰：「漢氏承秦，改六冕之制，但玄冠絳衣而已。

translations.literal: Wei palace library director Qin Jing said: “Han inherited Qin, changed the six-crown system, only black cap and crimson robe.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jing noted Han simplified Zhou’s six crowns to black cap and red robe.

sentences.zh: 」魏已來名為五時朝服，又有四時朝服，又有朝服。

translations.literal: ” From Wei onward it was named five-season court dress; moreover there was four-season court dress; moreover there was court dress.
translations.idiomatic: ” Wei–Jin codified “five-season” and “four-season” court wardrobes.

sentences.zh: 自皇太子以下隨官受給。

translations.literal: From the crown prince downward, each follows office to receive issue.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks down to the heir draw costumes by appointment.

sentences.zh: 百官雖服五時朝服，據今止給四時朝服，闕秋服。

translations.literal: Although the hundred officials wear five-season court dress, according to present practice they only issue four-season court dress, lacking autumn dress.
translations.idiomatic: Jin budgets skipped autumn palettes despite five-season theory.

sentences.zh: 三年一易。

translations.literal: Every three years one change.
translations.idiomatic: Sets renew triennially.

sentences.zh: 諸假印綬而官不給鞶囊者，得自具作，其但假印不假綬者，不得佩綬鞶，古制也。

translations.literal: For those lent seals and ribbons but offices do not issue pan pouches, they may make them themselves; for those only lent seals but not ribbons, they may not wear ribbon pan—ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: Acting officials without formal sashes may not wear ribbon belts.

sentences.zh: 漢世著鞶囊者，側在腰間，或謂之傍囊，或謂之綬囊，然則以紫囊盛綬也。
