translations.literal: For Han generations those wearing pan pouches placed them at the waist side; some called them side pouches, some called them ribbon pouches; thus they used purple pouches to hold ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: Han hung purple “side pouches” for credential tubes.

sentences.zh: 或盛或散，各有其時。

translations.literal: Sometimes full sometimes scattered, each has its season.
translations.idiomatic: Full or empty pouches followed seasonal rules.

sentences.zh: 笏，古者貴賤皆執笏，其有事則搢之於腰帶，所謂搢紳之士者，搢笏而垂紳帶也。

translations.literal: The tablet: in antiquity noble and base all held tablets; when there was business then they tucked them in the waist belt—what is called “tablet-girdle gentlemen” is tucking tablet while hanging sash belt.
translations.idiomatic: All ranks once carried hu tablets tucked in sashes—“gentry” literally meant tablet and sash.

sentences.zh: 紳垂長三尺。

translations.literal: The sash hangs three chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial sashes trail three chi.

sentences.zh: 笏者，有事則書之，故常簪筆，今之白筆是其遺象。

translations.literal: The tablet: when there was business then they wrote on it, therefore constantly pinned brush; today’s white brush is its surviving image.
translations.idiomatic: Tablets doubled as note boards—hence the white brush pin survives.

sentences.zh: 三台五省二品文官簪之，王、公、侯、伯、子、男、卿尹及武官不簪，加內侍位者乃簪之。

translations.literal: Three terraces five departments second-rank civil officials pin them; kings, dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, ministers and prefects and martial officials do not pin; only those who add inner attendant posts pin them.
translations.idiomatic: Only high civil bureaus and inner-court add-ons wear brush pins.

sentences.zh: 手版即古笏矣。

translations.literal: The hand tablet is the ancient hu.
translations.idiomatic: The board-shaped hu is the old tablet.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、僕射、尚書手版頭復有白筆，以紫皮裹之，名曰笏。

translations.literal: Masters of writing director, vice, masters of writing have white brush atop the hand tablet, wrapped in purple leather, called hu.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of state cap their hu with purple-sheathed white brushes.

sentences.zh: 皇太子金璽龜鈕，硃黃綬，四采：赤、黃、縹、紺。

translations.literal: The heir apparent’s gold seal tortoise knob, cinnabar-yellow sash, four colors: red, yellow, light blue, dark blue.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wears gold tortoise seal and four-hued sash.

sentences.zh: 給五時朝服、遠遊冠，介幘、翠緌。

translations.literal: Issued five-season court dress, far-roaming cap, stiff cap, kingfisher tassel.
translations.idiomatic: He receives five-season wardrobe, far-roaming cap, stiff ze, kingfisher fringe.

sentences.zh: 佩瑜玉，垂組。

translations.literal: Wearing fine jade, hanging cords.
translations.idiomatic: He wears flawless jade pendants on silk cords.

sentences.zh: 硃衣絳紗襮，皁緣白紗，其中衣白曲領。

translations.literal: Cinnabar robe crimson gauze half-arm, black-bordered white gauze, middle garment white curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet court robe over white gauze with black piping and curved collar.

sentences.zh: 帶劍，火珠素首。

translations.literal: Bearing sword, fire pearl plain hilt.
translations.idiomatic: He belts a sword with plain hilt and “fire pearl” ornament.

sentences.zh: 革帶，玉鉤燮獸頭鞶囊。

translations.literal: Leather belt, jade hook tile beast-head pan pouch.
translations.idiomatic: His belt uses jade hooks and beast-head pouch.

sentences.zh: 其大小會、祠宗廟、朔望、五日還朝皆朝服，常還上宮則硃服，預上宮正會則于殿下脫劍舄。

translations.literal: For great and small assemblies, sacrificing to the ancestral temple, new and full moons, fifth-day returns to court, all court dress; regularly returning to the upper palace then cinnabar dress; when attending upper palace great session then below the hall remove sword and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: He changes between full court, palace crimson, and disarmed hall dress by occasion.

sentences.zh: 又有三梁進賢冠。

translations.literal: Moreover there is three-ridge worthy-advancement cap.
translations.idiomatic: He also owns the three-ridge scholar cap.

sentences.zh: 其侍祀則平冕九旒，袞衣九章，白紗絳緣中單，絳繒韠，采畫織成袞帶，金辟邪首，紫綠二色帶，采畫廣領、曲領各一，赤舄絳襪。

translations.literal: When attending sacrifice then level crown nine tassels, nine-emblem sacrificial robe, white gauze crimson-bordered inner robe, crimson silk knee covers, woven five-color sacrificial belt, golden bixie beast head, purple and green two-color belt, painted broad collar and curved collar one each, red shoes crimson socks.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice calls for nine-tasseled flat crown, nine-dragon robe, layered sashes, and red footgear.

sentences.zh: 若講，則著介幘單衣。

translations.literal: If lecturing, then wear stiff cap unlined robe.
translations.idiomatic: For lectures he dons simple ze and robe.

sentences.zh: 釋奠，則遠遊冠，玄朝服，絳緣中單，絳袴襪，玄舄。

translations.literal: For school sacrifice to the former sage, then far-roaming cap, black court dress, crimson-bordered inner robe, crimson trousers and socks, black shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian rites use far-roaming cap and black ensemble.

sentences.zh: 若未加元服，則中舍人執冕從，介幘單衣玄服。

translations.literal: If he has not yet added the capping, then the household aide holds the crown following, stiff cap unlined robe black dress.
translations.idiomatic: Uncapped princes follow with an attendant carrying the mian crown while they wear black ze robes.

sentences.zh: 諸王金璽龜鈕，纁硃綬，四采：硃、黃、縹、紺。

translations.literal: Princes’ gold seal tortoise knob, reddish-cinnabar sash, four colors: cinnabar, yellow, light blue, dark blue.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the blood wear gold tortoise seals and four-color sashes.

sentences.zh: 五時朝服，遠遊冠介幘，亦有三梁進賢冠。

translations.literal: Five-season court dress, far-roaming cap stiff cap, also having three-ridge worthy-advancement cap.
translations.idiomatic: They mirror the heir’s wardrobe minus certain honors.

sentences.zh: 硃衣絳紗襮皁緣，中衣表素。

translations.literal: Cinnabar robe crimson gauze half-arm black border, middle garment surface plain.
translations.idiomatic: Their court coat pairs scarlet panels with plain underlayers.

sentences.zh: 革帶，黑舄，佩山玄玉，垂組，大帶。

translations.literal: Leather belt, black shoes, wearing mountain-dark jade, hanging cords, great sash.
translations.idiomatic: Black shoes, mountain-dark jade, and broad sash complete the look.

sentences.zh: 若加餘官，則服其加官之服也。

translations.literal: If additional offices are added, then wear the added office’s dress.
translations.idiomatic: Extra titles bring matching uniforms.

sentences.zh: 皇后謁廟，其服皁上皁下，親蠶則青上縹下，皆深衣制，隱領，袖緣以絛。

translations.literal: When the empress visits the temple, her dress is black above and black below; for personal silkworm then green above and light blue below; all deep-robe system, hidden collar, cuffs bordered with tape.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wears deep black for temples, green-blue for silkworm, piped deep robes.

sentences.zh: 首飾則假髻，步搖，俗謂之珠松是也，簪珥。

translations.literal: For head ornaments then false topknot, buyao, vulgarly called pearl pine is this, hairpins and earrings.
translations.idiomatic: Her hair uses false chignons, buyao tremblers, pins, and earrings.

sentences.zh: 步搖以黃金為山題，貫白珠為支相繆。

translations.literal: The buyao uses gold for mountain title, piercing white pearls as branches intertwining.
translations.idiomatic: Buyao frames are golden “mountains” strung with white pearls.

sentences.zh: 八爵九華，熊、獸、赤羆、天鹿、辟邪、南山豐大特六獸，諸爵獸皆以翡翠為毛羽，金題白珠榼，繞以翡翠為華。

translations.literal: Eight sparrows nine blossoms, bear, beast, red bear, heavenly deer, bixie, southern mountain great boar six beasts; the various sparrow beasts all use kingfisher for feathers and fur, gold title white pearl cups, wound with kingfisher for blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: The crown bristles with jeweled birds and beasts—sparrows, bears, deer, exorcist lions—all feathered in kingfisher and gold.

sentences.zh: 元康六年，詔曰：「魏以來皇后蠶服皆以文繡，非古義也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuankang, an edict said: “Since Wei, empresses’ silkworm dress has all used patterned embroidery; it is not ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang six decreed that brocade silkworm gowns broke classical sobriety.

sentences.zh: 今宜純服青，以為永制。」

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to wear pure green, taking it as permanent regulation.”
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth empresses would wear plain green at silkworm.

sentences.zh: 貴人、夫人、貴嬪，是為三夫人，皆金章紫綬，章文曰貴人、夫人、貴嬪之章。

translations.literal: Honored lady, lady, honored concubine—these are the three consorts; all have gold seal purple sash; the seal text says honored lady, lady, honored concubine seals.
translations.idiomatic: The three chief consorts carry gold seals on purple ribbons.

sentences.zh: 佩于闐玉。

translations.literal: They wear Khotan jade.
translations.idiomatic: They mount Khotan jade pendants.

sentences.zh: 淑妃、淑媛、淑儀、修華、修容、修儀、婕妤、容華、充華，是為九嬪，銀印青綬，佩采瓄玉。

translations.literal: Virtuous consort, virtuous beauty, virtuous deportment, cultivated splendor, cultivated countenance, cultivated deportment, lady of bright deportment, splendor countenance, filling splendor—these are the nine concubines; silver seal blue sash, wearing patterned jade.
translations.idiomatic: Nine ranks of concubines wear silver seals, blue sashes, and mottled jade.

sentences.zh: 貴人、貴嬪、夫人助蠶，服純縹為上與下，皆深衣制。

translations.literal: Honored lady, honored concubine, and lady assisting at silkworm wear pure light blue above and below, all deep-robe system.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ladies at the silkworm rite wear monochrome blue deep robes.

sentences.zh: 太平髻，七䥖蔽髻，黑玳瑁，又加簪珥。

translations.literal: Great peace topknot, seven-pin covering topknot, black tortoiseshell, again adding hairpins and earrings.
translations.idiomatic: Their hair towers in “great peace” buns with seven pins and tortoiseshell frames.

sentences.zh: 九嬪及公主、夫人五䥖，世婦三䥖。

translations.literal: Nine concubines and princesses and ladies five pins, noble wives three pins.
translations.idiomatic: Pin counts drop by rank—five or three jeweled skewers.

sentences.zh: 助蠶之義，自古而然矣。

translations.literal: The meaning of assisting silkworm has been thus from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworm assistance is an immemorial duty of palace women.

sentences.zh: 皇太子妃金璽龜鈕，纁硃綬，佩瑜玉。

translations.literal: The heir apparent’s consort gold seal tortoise knob, reddish-cinnabar sash, wearing fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: The crown princess matches princes’ tortoise seal and sash with fine jade.

sentences.zh: 諸王太妃、妃、諸長公主、公主、封君金印紫綬，佩山玄玉。

translations.literal: Princes’ grand consorts and consorts, various senior princesses and princesses, and enfeoffed noblewomen have gold seal purple sash, wearing mountain-dark jade.
translations.idiomatic: Princely consorts and titled princesses share gold-on-purple with dark jade.

sentences.zh: 長公主、公主見會，太平髻，七䥖蔽髻。

translations.literal: Senior princesses and princesses at meetings, great peace topknot, seven-pin covering topknot.
translations.idiomatic: At audiences princesses don the great-peace bun with seven jeweled pins.

sentences.zh: 其長公主得有步搖，皆有簪珥，衣服同制。

translations.literal: Their senior princesses may obtain buyao; all have hairpins and earrings; clothes share the same system.
translations.idiomatic: Senior princesses who earn buyao tremblers also receive pins and earrings under the same wardrobe code.

sentences.zh: 自公主、封君以上皆帶綬，以彩組為緄帶，各如其綬色，金辟邪首為帶玦。

translations.literal: From princesses and enfeoffed noblewomen upward all wear sashes; using colored cords as edge bands, each matching its sash color; golden bixie head as belt ring.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and titled noblewomen belt formal sashes with color-matched cord trim and gilded bixie belt toggles.

sentences.zh: 郡公侯縣公侯太夫人，夫人銀印青綬，佩水蒼玉，其特加乃金紫。

translations.literal: Commandery dukes and marquises’ and county dukes’ and marquises’ grand ladies and ladies have silver seal blue sash, wearing water-green jade; if specially advanced then gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: County and commandery ducal consorts normally wear silver on blue with aquamarine jade, unless promoted to gold-and-purple honors.

sentences.zh: 公特進侯卿校世婦、中二千石二千石夫人紺繒幗，黃金龍首銜白珠，魚須擿長一尺為簪珥。

translations.literal: Dukes fully eminent, marquises, ministers, colonels’ chief wives, and wives at full and regular two thousand piculs wear dark silk headcloths, yellow gold dragon heads holding white pearls, fish-whisker plucks one chi long as hairpins and earrings.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers’ wives don dark gauze caps with gold dragon friezes, white pearls, and foot-long “fish-whisker” pins as earrings.

sentences.zh: 入廟佐祭者皁絹上下。

translations.literal: Those who enter the temple assisting sacrifice wear black silk above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Women assisting temple sacrifice wear all-black silk deep robes.

sentences.zh: 助蠶者縹絹上下，皆深衣制緣。

translations.literal: Those assisting silkworm wear light-blue silk above and below, all deep-robe system with borders.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworm helpers wear bordered light-blue deep gowns.

sentences.zh: 自二千石夫人以上至皇后，皆以蠶衣為朝服。

translations.literal: From two thousand piculs’ wives upward to the empress, all take silkworm dress as court dress.
translations.idiomatic: From senior ministers’ wives to the empress, formal court dress means the silkworm vestment set.
